text: A wise son maketh a glad father; But a foolish man despiseth his mother.

title: Proverbs 15:21
text: Folly is joy to him that is void of wisdom; But a man of understanding maketh straight his going.

title: Proverbs 15:22
text: Where there is no counsel, purposes are disappointed; But in the multitude of counsellors they are established.

title: Proverbs 15:23
text: A man hath joy in the answer of his mouth; And a word in due season, how good is it!

title: Proverbs 15:24
text: To the wise the way of life [goeth] upward, That he may depart from Sheol beneath.

title: Proverbs 15:25
text: Jehovah will root up the house of the proud; But he will establish the border of the widow.

title: Proverbs 15:26
text: Evil devices are an abomination to Jehovah; But pleasant words [are] pure.

title: Proverbs 15:27
text: He that is greedy of gain troubleth his own house; But he that hateth bribes shall live.

title: Proverbs 15:28
text: The heart of the righteous studieth to answer; But the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things.

title: Proverbs 15:29
text: Jehovah is far from the wicked; But he heareth the prayer of the righteous.

title: Proverbs 15:30
text: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart; [And] good tidings make the bones fat.

title: Proverbs 15:31
text: The ear that hearkeneth to the reproof of life Shall abide among the wise.

title: Proverbs 15:32
text: He that refuseth correction despiseth his own soul; But he that hearkeneth to reproof getteth understanding.

title: Proverbs 15:33
text: The fear of Jehovah is the instruction of wisdom; And before honor [goeth] humility.

title: Proverbs 16:1
text: The plans of the heart belong to man; But the answer of the tongue is from Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 16:2
text: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; But Jehovah weigheth the spirits.

title: Proverbs 16:3
text: Commit thy works unto Jehovah, And thy purposes shall be established.

title: Proverbs 16:4
text: Jehovah hath made everything for its own end; Yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.

title: Proverbs 16:5
text: Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to Jehovah: [Though] hand [join] in hand, he shall not be unpunished.

title: Proverbs 16:6
text: By mercy and truth iniquity is atoned for; And by the fear of Jehovah men depart from evil.

title: Proverbs 16:7
text: When a man's ways please Jehovah, He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.

title: Proverbs 16:8
text: Better is a little, with righteousness, Than great revenues with injustice.

title: Proverbs 16:9
text: A man's heart deviseth his way; But Jehovah directeth his steps.

title: Proverbs 16:10
text: A divine sentence is in the lips of the king; His mouth shall not transgress in judgment.

title: Proverbs 16:11
text: A just balance and scales are Jehovah's; All the weights of the bag are his work.

title: Proverbs 16:12
text: It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness; For the throne is established by righteousness.

title: Proverbs 16:13
text: Righteous lips are the delight of kings; And they love him that speaketh right.

title: Proverbs 16:14
text: The wrath of a king is [as] messengers of death; But a wise man will pacify it.

title: Proverbs 16:15
text: In the light of the king's countenance is life; And his favor is as a cloud of the latter rain.

title: Proverbs 16:16
text: How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! Yea, to get understanding is rather to be chosen than silver.

title: Proverbs 16:17
text: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil: He that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.

title: Proverbs 16:18
text: Pride [goeth] before destruction, And a haughty spirit before a fall.

title: Proverbs 16:19
text: Better it is to be of a lowly spirit with the poor, Than to divide the spoil with the proud.

title: Proverbs 16:20
text: He that giveth heed unto the word shall find good; And whoso trusteth in Jehovah, happy is he.

title: Proverbs 16:21
text: The wise in heart shall be called prudent; And the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning.

title: Proverbs 16:22
text: Understanding is a well-spring of life unto him that hath it; But the correction of fools is [their] folly.

title: Proverbs 16:23
text: The heart of the wise instructeth his mouth, And addeth learning to his lips.

title: Proverbs 16:24
text: Pleasant words are [as] a honeycomb, Sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.

title: Proverbs 16:25
text: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, But the end thereof are the ways of death.

title: Proverbs 16:26
text: The appetite of the laboring man laboreth for him; For his mouth urgeth him [thereto] .

title: Proverbs 16:27
text: A worthless man deviseth mischief; And in his lips there is as a scorching fire.

title: Proverbs 16:28
text: A perverse man scattereth abroad strife; And a whisperer separateth chief friends.

title: Proverbs 16:29
text: A man of violence enticeth his neighbor, And leadeth him in a way that is not good.

title: Proverbs 16:30
text: He that shutteth his eyes, [it is] to devise perverse things: He that compresseth his lips bringeth evil to pass.

title: Proverbs 16:31
text: The hoary head is a crown of glory; It shall be found in the way of righteousness.

title: Proverbs 16:32
text: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; And he that ruleth his spirit, than he that taketh a city.

title: Proverbs 16:33
text: The lot is cast into the lap; But the whole disposing thereof is of Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 17:1
text: Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, Than a house full of feasting with strife.

title: Proverbs 17:2
text: A servant that dealeth wisely shall have rule over a son that causeth shame, And shall have part in the inheritance among the brethren.

title: Proverbs 17:3
text: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; But Jehovah trieth the hearts.

title: Proverbs 17:4
text: An evil-doer giveth heed to wicked lips; [And] a liar giveth ear to a mischievous tongue.

title: Proverbs 17:5
text: Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker; [And] he that is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished.

title: Proverbs 17:6
text: Children's children are the crown of old men; And the glory of children are their fathers.

title: Proverbs 17:7
text: Excellent speech becometh not a fool; Much less do lying lips a prince.

title: Proverbs 17:8
text: A bribe is [as] a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it; Whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.

title: Proverbs 17:9
text: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; But he that harpeth on a matter separateth chief friends.

title: Proverbs 17:10
text: A rebuke entereth deeper into one that hath understanding Than a hundred stripes into a fool.

title: Proverbs 17:11
text: An evil man seeketh only rebellion; Therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.

title: Proverbs 17:12
text: Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man, Rather than a fool in his folly.

title: Proverbs 17:13
text: Whoso rewardeth evil for good, Evil shall not depart from his house.

title: Proverbs 17:14
text: The beginning of strife is [as] when one letteth out water: Therefore leave off contention, before there is quarrelling.

title: Proverbs 17:15
text: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the righteous, Both of them alike are an abomination to Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 17:16
text: Wherefore is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, Seeing he hath no understanding?

title: Proverbs 17:17
text: A friend loveth at all times; And a brother is born for adversity.

title: Proverbs 17:18
text: A man void of understanding striketh hands, And becometh surety in the presence of his neighbor.

title: Proverbs 17:19
text: He loveth transgression that loveth strife: He that raiseth high his gate seeketh destruction.

title: Proverbs 17:20
text: He that hath a wayward heart findeth no good; And he that hath a perverse tongue falleth into mischief.

title: Proverbs 17:21
text: He that begetteth a fool [doeth it] to his sorrow; And the father of a fool hath no joy.

title: Proverbs 17:22
text: A cheerful heart is a good medicine; But a broken spirit drieth up the bones.

title: Proverbs 17:23
text: A wicked man receiveth a bribe out of the bosom, To pervert the ways of justice.

title: Proverbs 17:24
text: Wisdom is before the face of him that hath understanding; But the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.

title: Proverbs 17:25
text: A foolish son is a grief to his father, And bitterness to her that bare him.

title: Proverbs 17:26
text: Also to punish the righteous is not good, [Nor] to smite the noble for [their] uprightness.

title: Proverbs 17:27
text: He that spareth his words hath knowledge; And he that is of a cool spirit is a man of understanding.

title: Proverbs 17:28
text: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise; When he shutteth his lips, he is [esteemed as] prudent.

title: Proverbs 18:1
text: He that separateth himself seeketh [his own] desire, And rageth against all sound wisdom.

title: Proverbs 18:2
text: A fool hath no delight in understanding, But only that his heart may reveal itself.

title: Proverbs 18:3
text: When the wicked cometh, there cometh also contempt, And with ignominy [cometh] reproach.

title: Proverbs 18:4
text: The words of a man's mouth are [as] deep waters; The wellspring of wisdom is [as] a flowing brook.

title: Proverbs 18:5
text: To respect the person of the wicked is not good, [Nor] to turn aside the righteous in judgment.

title: Proverbs 18:6
text: A fool's lips enter into contention, And his mouth calleth for stripes.

title: Proverbs 18:7
text: A fool's mouth is his destruction, And his lips are the snare of his soul.

title: Proverbs 18:8
text: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, And they go down into the innermost parts.

title: Proverbs 18:9
text: He also that is slack in his work Is brother to him that is a destroyer.

title: Proverbs 18:10
text: The name of Jehovah is a strong tower; The righteous runneth into it, and is safe.

title: Proverbs 18:11
text: The rich man's wealth is his strong city, And as a high wall in his own imagination.

title: Proverbs 18:12
text: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty; And before honor [goeth] humility.

title: Proverbs 18:13
text: He that giveth answer before he heareth, It is folly and shame unto him.

title: Proverbs 18:14
text: The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; But a broken spirit who can bear?

title: Proverbs 18:15
text: The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; And the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.

title: Proverbs 18:16
text: A man's gift maketh room for him, And bringeth him before great men.

title: Proverbs 18:17
text: He that pleadeth his cause first [seemeth] just; But his neighbor cometh and searcheth him out.

title: Proverbs 18:18
text: The lot causeth contentions to cease, And parteth between the mighty.

title: Proverbs 18:19
text: A brother offended [is harder to be won] than a strong city; And [such] contentions are like the bars of a castle.

title: Proverbs 18:20
text: A man's belly shall be filled with the fruit of his mouth; With the increase of his lips shall he be satisfied.

title: Proverbs 18:21
text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; And they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

title: Proverbs 18:22
text: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, And obtaineth favor of Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 18:23
text: The poor useth entreaties; But the rich answereth roughly.

title: Proverbs 18:24
text: He that maketh many friends [doeth it] to his own destruction; But there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.

title: Proverbs 19:1
text: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity Than he that is perverse in his lips and is a fool.

title: Proverbs 19:2
text: Also, that the soul be without knowledge is not good; And he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.

title: Proverbs 19:3
text: The foolishness of man subverteth his way; And his heart fretteth against Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 19:4
text: Wealth addeth many friends; But the poor is separated from his friend.

title: Proverbs 19:5
text: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall not escape.

title: Proverbs 19:6
text: Many will entreat the favor of the liberal man; And every man is a friend to him that giveth gifts.

title: Proverbs 19:7
text: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: How much more do his friends go far from him! He pursueth [them with] words, [but] they are gone.

title: Proverbs 19:8
text: He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: He that keepeth understanding shall find good.

title: Proverbs 19:9
text: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall perish.

title: Proverbs 19:10
text: Delicate living is not seemly for a fool; Much less for a servant to have rule over princes.

title: Proverbs 19:11
text: The discretion of a man maketh him slow to anger; And it is his glory to pass over a transgression.

title: Proverbs 19:12
text: The king's wrath is as the roaring of a lion; But his favor is as dew upon the grass.

title: Proverbs 19:13
text: A foolish son is the calamity of his father; And the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.

title: Proverbs 19:14
text: House and riches are an inheritance from fathers; But a prudent wife is from Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 19:15
text: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; And the idle soul shall suffer hunger.

title: Proverbs 19:16
text: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his soul; [But] he that is careless of his ways shall die.

title: Proverbs 19:17
text: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Jehovah, And his good deed will he pay him again.

title: Proverbs 19:18
text: Chasten thy son, seeing there is hope; And set not thy heart on his destruction.

title: Proverbs 19:19
text: A man of great wrath shall bear the penalty; For if thou deliver [him], thou must do it yet again.

title: Proverbs 19:20
text: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, That thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.

title: Proverbs 19:21
text: There are many devices in a man's heart; But the counsel of Jehovah, that shall stand.

title: Proverbs 19:22
text: That which maketh a man to be desired is his kindness; And a poor man is better than a liar.

title: Proverbs 19:23
text: The fear of Jehovah [tendeth] to life; And he [that hath it] shall abide satisfied; He shall not be visited with evil.

title: Proverbs 19:24
text: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish, And will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.

title: Proverbs 19:25
text: Smite a scoffer, and the simple will learn prudence; And reprove one that hath understanding, [and] he will understand knowledge.

title: Proverbs 19:26
text: He that doeth violence to his father, and chaseth away his mother, Is a son that causeth shame and bringeth reproach.

title: Proverbs 19:27
text: Cease, my son, to hear instruction [Only] to err from the words of knowledge.

title: Proverbs 19:28
text: A worthless witness mocketh at justice; And the mouth of the wicked swalloweth iniquity.

title: Proverbs 19:29
text: Judgments are prepared for scoffers, And stripes for the back of fools.

title: Proverbs 20:1
text: Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler; And whosoever erreth thereby is not wise.

title: Proverbs 20:2
text: The terror of a king is as the roaring of a lion: He that provoketh him to anger sinneth [against] his own life.

title: Proverbs 20:3
text: It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife; But every fool will be quarrelling.

title: Proverbs 20:4
text: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the winter; Therefore he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.

title: Proverbs 20:5
text: Counsel in the heart of man is [like] deep water; But a man of understanding will draw it out.

title: Proverbs 20:6
text: Most men will proclaim every one his own kindness; But a faithful man who can find?

title: Proverbs 20:7
text: A righteous man that walketh in his integrity, Blessed are his children after him.

title: Proverbs 20:8
text: A king that sitteth on the throne of judgment Scattereth away all evil with his eyes.

title: Proverbs 20:9
text: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?

title: Proverbs 20:10
text: Diverse weights, and diverse measures, Both of them alike are an abomination to Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 20:11
text: Even a child maketh himself known by his doings, Whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.

title: Proverbs 20:12
text: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Jehovah hath made even both of them.

title: Proverbs 20:13
text: Love not sleep, let thou come to poverty; Open thine eyes, [and] thou shalt be satisfied with bread.

title: Proverbs 20:14
text: It is bad, it is bad, saith the buyer; But when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.

title: Proverbs 20:15
text: There is gold, and abundance of rubies; But the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.

title: Proverbs 20:16
text: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge [that is surety] for foreigners.

title: Proverbs 20:17
text: Bread of falsehood is sweet to a man; But afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.

title: Proverbs 20:18
text: Every purpose is established by counsel; And by wise guidance make thou war.

title: Proverbs 20:19
text: He that goeth about as a tale-bearer revealeth secrets; Therefore company not with him that openeth wide his lips.

title: Proverbs 20:20
text: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, His lamp shall be put out in blackness of darkness.

title: Proverbs 20:21
text: An inheritance [may be] gotten hastily at the beginning; But the end thereof shall not be blessed.

title: Proverbs 20:22
text: Say not thou, I will recompense evil: Wait for Jehovah, and he will save thee.

title: Proverbs 20:23
text: Diverse weights are an abomination to Jehovah; And a false balance is not good.

title: Proverbs 20:24
text: A man's goings are of Jehovah; How then can man understand his way?

title: Proverbs 20:25
text: It is a snare to a man rashly to say, [It is] holy, And after vows to make inquiry.

title: Proverbs 20:26
text: A wise king winnoweth the wicked, And bringeth the [threshing] -wheel over them.

title: Proverbs 20:27
text: The spirit of man is the lamp of Jehovah, Searching all his innermost parts.

title: Proverbs 20:28
text: Kindness and truth preserve the king; And his throne is upholden by kindness.

title: Proverbs 20:29
text: The glory of young men is their strength; And the beauty of old men is the hoary head.

title: Proverbs 20:30
text: Stripes that wound cleanse away evil; And strokes [reach] the innermost parts.

title: Proverbs 21:1
text: The king's heart is in the hand of Jehovah as the watercourses: He turneth it whithersoever he will.

title: Proverbs 21:2
text: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes; But Jehovah weigheth the hearts.

title: Proverbs 21:3
text: To do righteousness and justice Is more acceptable to Jehovah than sacrifice.

title: Proverbs 21:4
text: A high look, and a proud heart, [Even] the lamp of the wicked, is sin.

title: Proverbs 21:5
text: The thoughts of the diligent [tend] only to plenteousness; But every one that is hasty [hasteth] only to want.

title: Proverbs 21:6
text: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue Is a vapor driven to and fro by them that seek death.

title: Proverbs 21:7
text: The violence of the wicked shall sweep them away, Because they refuse to do justice.

title: Proverbs 21:8
text: The way of him that is laden with guilt is exceeding crooked; But as for the pure, his work is right.

title: Proverbs 21:9
text: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.

title: Proverbs 21:10
text: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: His neighbor findeth no favor in his eyes.

title: Proverbs 21:11
text: When the scoffer is punished, the simple is made wise; And when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.

title: Proverbs 21:12
text: The righteous man considereth the house of the wicked, [How] the wicked are overthrown to [their] ruin.

title: Proverbs 21:13
text: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, He also shall cry, but shall not be heard.

title: Proverbs 21:14
text: A gift in secret pacifieth anger; And a present in the bosom, strong wrath.

title: Proverbs 21:15
text: It is joy to the righteous to do justice; But it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.

title: Proverbs 21:16
text: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding Shall rest in the assembly of the dead.

title: Proverbs 21:17
text: He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: He that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.

title: Proverbs 21:18
text: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous; And the treacherous [cometh] in the stead of the upright.

title: Proverbs 21:19
text: It is better to dwell in a desert land, Than with a contentious and fretful woman.

title: Proverbs 21:20
text: There is precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise; But a foolish man swalloweth it up.

title: Proverbs 21:21
text: He that followeth after righteousness and kindness Findeth life, righteousness, and honor.

title: Proverbs 21:22
text: A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty, And bringeth down the strength of the confidence thereof.

title: Proverbs 21:23
text: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue Keepeth his soul from troubles.

title: Proverbs 21:24
text: The proud and haughty man, scoffer is his name; He worketh in the arrogance of pride.

title: Proverbs 21:25
text: The desire of the sluggard killeth him; For his hands refuse to labor.

title: Proverbs 21:26
text: There is that coveteth greedily all the day long; But the righteous giveth and withholdeth not.

title: Proverbs 21:27
text: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination: How much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind!

title: Proverbs 21:28
text: A false witness shall perish; But the man that heareth shall speak so as to endure.

title: Proverbs 21:29
text: A wicked man hardeneth his face; But as for the upright, he establisheth his ways.

title: Proverbs 21:30
text: There is no wisdom nor understanding Nor counsel against Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 21:31
text: The horse is prepared against the day of battle; But victory is of Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 22:1
text: A [good] name is rather to be chosen than great riches, [And] loving favor rather than silver and gold.

title: Proverbs 22:2
text: The rich and the poor meet together: Jehovah is the maker of them all.

title: Proverbs 22:3
text: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself; But the simple pass on, and suffer for it.

title: Proverbs 22:4
text: The reward of humility [and] the fear of Jehovah [Is] riches, and honor, and life.

title: Proverbs 22:5
text: Thorns [and] snares are in the way of the perverse: He that keepeth his soul shall be far from them.

title: Proverbs 22:6
text: Train up a child in the way he should go, And even when he is old he will not depart from it.

title: Proverbs 22:7
text: The rich ruleth over the poor; And the borrower is servant to the lender.

title: Proverbs 22:8
text: He that soweth iniquity shall reap calamity; And the rod of his wrath shall fail.

title: Proverbs 22:9
text: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; For he giveth of his bread to the poor.

title: Proverbs 22:10
text: Cast out the scoffer, and contention will go out; Yea, strife and ignominy will cease.

title: Proverbs 22:11
text: He that loveth pureness of heart, [For] the grace of his lips the king will be his friend.

title: Proverbs 22:12
text: The eyes of Jehovah preserve [him that hath] knowledge; But he overthroweth the words of the treacherous man.

title: Proverbs 22:13
text: The sluggard saith, There is a lion without: I shall be slain in the streets.

title: Proverbs 22:14
text: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit: He that is abhorred of Jehovah shall fall therein.

title: Proverbs 22:15
text: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child; [But] the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.

title: Proverbs 22:16
text: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his [gain], [And] he that giveth to the rich, [shall come] only to want.

title: Proverbs 22:17
text: Incline thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, And apply thy heart unto my knowledge.

title: Proverbs 22:18
text: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee, If they be established together upon thy lips.

title: Proverbs 22:19
text: That thy trust may be in Jehovah, I have made [them] known to thee this day, even to thee.

title: Proverbs 22:20
text: Have not I written unto thee excellent things Of counsels and knowledge,

title: Proverbs 22:21
text: To make thee know the certainty of the words of truth, That thou mayest carry back words of truth to them that send thee?

title: Proverbs 22:22
text: Rob not the poor, because he is poor; Neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:

title: Proverbs 22:23
text: For Jehovah will plead their cause, And despoil of life those that despoil them.

title: Proverbs 22:24
text: Make no friendship with a man that is given to anger; And with a wrathful man thou shalt not go:

title: Proverbs 22:25
text: Lest thou learn this ways, And get a snare to thy soul.

title: Proverbs 22:26
text: Be thou not one of them that strike hands, [Or] of them that are sureties for debts.

title: Proverbs 22:27
text: If thou hast not wherewith to pay, Why should he take away thy bed from under thee?

title: Proverbs 22:28
text: Remove not the ancient landmark, Which thy fathers have set.

title: Proverbs 22:29
text: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; He shall not stand before mean men.

title: Proverbs 23:1
text: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, Consider diligently him that is before thee;

title: Proverbs 23:2
text: And put a knife to thy throat, If thou be a man given to appetite.

title: Proverbs 23:3
text: Be not desirous of his dainties; Seeing they are deceitful food.

title: Proverbs 23:4
text: Weary not thyself to be rich; Cease from thine own wisdom.

title: Proverbs 23:5
text: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? For [riches] certainly make themselves wings, Like an eagle that flieth toward heaven.

title: Proverbs 23:6
text: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, Neither desire thou his dainties:

title: Proverbs 23:7
text: For as he thinketh within himself, so is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; But his heart is not with thee.

title: Proverbs 23:8
text: The morsel which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, And lose thy sweet words.

title: Proverbs 23:9
text: Speak not in the hearing of a fool; For he will despise the wisdom of thy words.

title: Proverbs 23:10
text: Remove not the ancient landmark; And enter not into the fields of the fatherless:

title: Proverbs 23:11
text: For their Redeemer is strong; He will plead their cause against thee.

title: Proverbs 23:12
text: Apply thy heart unto instruction, And thine ears to the words of knowledge.

title: Proverbs 23:13
text: Withhold not correction from the child; [For] if thou beat him with the rod, he will not die.

title: Proverbs 23:14
text: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, And shalt deliver his soul from Sheol.

title: Proverbs 23:15
text: My son, if thy heart be wise, My heart will be glad, even mine:

title: Proverbs 23:16
text: Yea, my heart will rejoice, When thy lips speak right things.

title: Proverbs 23:17
text: Let not thy heart envy sinners; But [be thou] in the fear of Jehovah all the day long:

title: Proverbs 23:18
text: For surely there is a reward; And thy hope shall not be cut off.

title: Proverbs 23:19
text: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, And guide thy heart in the way.

title: Proverbs 23:20
text: Be not among winebibbers, Among gluttonous eaters of flesh:

title: Proverbs 23:21
text: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty; And drowsiness will clothe [a man] with rags.

title: Proverbs 23:22
text: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, And despise not thy mother when she is old.

title: Proverbs 23:23
text: Buy the truth, and sell it not; [Yea], wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.

title: Proverbs 23:24
text: The father of the righteous will greatly rejoice; And he that begetteth a wise child will have joy of him.

title: Proverbs 23:25
text: Let thy father and thy mother be glad, And let her that bare thee rejoice.

title: Proverbs 23:26
text: My son, give me thy heart; And let thine eyes delight in my ways.

title: Proverbs 23:27
text: For a harlot is a deep ditch; And a foreign woman is a narrow pit.

title: Proverbs 23:28
text: Yea, she lieth in wait as a robber, And increaseth the treacherous among men.

title: Proverbs 23:29
text: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? Who hath complaining? who hath wounds without cause? Who hath redness of eyes?

title: Proverbs 23:30
text: They that tarry long at the wine; They that go to seek out mixed wine.

title: Proverbs 23:31
text: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, When it sparkleth in the cup, When it goeth down smoothly:

title: Proverbs 23:32
text: At the last it biteth like a serpent, And stingeth like an adder.

title: Proverbs 23:33
text: Thine eyes shall behold strange things, And thy heart shall utter perverse things.

title: Proverbs 23:34
text: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, Or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.

title: Proverbs 23:35
text: They have stricken me, [shalt thou say], and I was not hurt; They have beaten me, and I felt it not: When shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.

title: Proverbs 24:1
text: Be not thou envious against evil men; Neither desire to be with them:

title: Proverbs 24:2
text: For their heart studieth oppression, And their lips talk of mischief.

title: Proverbs 24:3
text: Through wisdom is a house builded; And by understanding it is established;

title: Proverbs 24:4
text: And by knowledge are the chambers filled With all precious and pleasant riches.

title: Proverbs 24:5
text: A wise man is strong; Yea, a man of knowledge increaseth might.

title: Proverbs 24:6
text: For by wise guidance thou shalt make thy war; And in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

title: Proverbs 24:7
text: Wisdom is too high for a fool: He openeth not his mouth in the gate.

title: Proverbs 24:8
text: He that deviseth to do evil, Men shall call him a mischief-maker.

title: Proverbs 24:9
text: The thought of foolishness is sin; And the scoffer is an abomination to men.

title: Proverbs 24:10
text: If thou faint in the day of adversity, Thy strength is small.

title: Proverbs 24:11
text: Deliver them that are carried away unto death, And those that are ready to be slain see that thou hold back.

title: Proverbs 24:12
text: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew not this; Doth not he that weigheth the hearts consider it? And he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? And shall not he render to every man according to his work?

title: Proverbs 24:13
text: My son, eat thou honey, for it is good; And the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to thy taste:

title: Proverbs 24:14
text: So shalt thou know wisdom to be unto thy soul; If thou hast found it, then shall there be a reward, And thy hope shall not be cut off.

title: Proverbs 24:15
text: Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous; Destroy not his resting-place:

title: Proverbs 24:16
text: For a righteous man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; But the wicked are overthrown by calamity.

title: Proverbs 24:17
text: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, And let not thy heart be glad when he is overthrown;

title: Proverbs 24:18
text: Lest Jehovah see it, and it displease him, And he turn away his wrath from him.

title: Proverbs 24:19
text: Fret not thyself because of evil-doers; Neither be thou envious at the wicked:

title: Proverbs 24:20
text: For there shall be no reward to the evil man; The lamp of the wicked shall be put out.

title: Proverbs 24:21
text: My son, fear thou Jehovah and the king; [And] company not with them that are given to change:

title: Proverbs 24:22
text: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; And the destruction from them both, who knoweth it?

title: Proverbs 24:23
text: These also are [sayings] of the wise. To have respect of persons in judgment is not good.

title: Proverbs 24:24
text: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous; Peoples shall curse him, nations shall abhor him:

title: Proverbs 24:25
text: But to them that rebuke [him] shall be delight, And a good blessing shall come upon them.

title: Proverbs 24:26
text: He kisseth the lips Who giveth a right answer.

title: Proverbs 24:27
text: Prepare thy work without, And make it ready for thee in the field; And afterwards build thy house.

title: Proverbs 24:28
text: Be not a witness against thy neighbor without cause; And deceive not with thy lips.

title: Proverbs 24:29
text: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me; I will render to the man according to his work.

title: Proverbs 24:30
text: I went by the field of the sluggard, And by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;

title: Proverbs 24:31
text: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, The face thereof was covered with nettles, And the stone wall thereof was broken down.

title: Proverbs 24:32
text: Then I beheld, and considered well; I saw, and received instruction:

title: Proverbs 24:33
text: [ Yet] a little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to sleep;

title: Proverbs 24:34
text: So shall thy poverty come as a robber, And thy want as an armed man.

title: Proverbs 25:1
text: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

title: Proverbs 25:2
text: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing; But the glory of kings is to search out a matter.

title: Proverbs 25:3
text: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, So the heart of kings is unsearchable.

title: Proverbs 25:4
text: Take away the dross from the silver, And there cometh forth a vessel for the refiner:

title: Proverbs 25:5
text: Take away the wicked [from] before the king, And his throne shall be established in righteousness.

title: Proverbs 25:6
text: Put not thyself forward in the presence of the king, And stand not in the place of great men:

title: Proverbs 25:7
text: For better is it that it be said unto thee, Come up hither, Than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince, Whom thine eyes have seen.

title: Proverbs 25:8
text: Go not forth hastily to strive, Lest [thou know not] what to do in the end thereof, When thy neighbor hath put thee to shame.

title: Proverbs 25:9
text: Debate thy cause with thy neighbor [himself], And disclose not the secret of another;

title: Proverbs 25:10
text: Lest he that heareth it revile thee, And thine infamy turn not away.

title: Proverbs 25:11
text: A word fitly spoken Is [like] apples of gold in network of silver.

title: Proverbs 25:12
text: [ As] an ear-ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, [So is] a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.

title: Proverbs 25:13
text: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, [So is] a faithful messenger to them that send him; For he refresheth the soul of his masters.

title: Proverbs 25:14
text: [ As] clouds and wind without rain, [So is] he that boasteth himself of his gifts falsely.

title: Proverbs 25:15
text: By long forbearing is a ruler persuaded, And a soft tongue breaketh the bone.

title: Proverbs 25:16
text: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, Lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.

title: Proverbs 25:17
text: Let thy foot be seldom in thy neighbor's house, Lest he be weary of thee, and hate thee.

title: Proverbs 25:18
text: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbor Is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.

title: Proverbs 25:19
text: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble Is [like] a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.

title: Proverbs 25:20
text: [ As] one that taketh off a garment in cold weather, [and as] vinegar upon soda, So is he that singeth songs to a heavy heart.

title: Proverbs 25:21
text: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; And if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

title: Proverbs 25:22
text: For thou wilt heap coals of fire upon his head, And Jehovah will reward thee.

title: Proverbs 25:23
text: The north wind bringeth forth rain: So doth a backbiting tongue an angry countenance.

title: Proverbs 25:24
text: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.

title: Proverbs 25:25
text: [ As] cold waters to a thirsty soul, So is good news from a far country.

title: Proverbs 25:26
text: [ As] a troubled fountain, and a corrupted spring, [So is] a righteous man that giveth way before the wicked.

title: Proverbs 25:27
text: It is not good to eat much honey: So [for men] to search out their own glory is grievous.

title: Proverbs 25:28
text: He whose spirit is without restraint Is [like] a city that is broken down and without walls.

title: Proverbs 26:1
text: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, So honor is not seemly for a fool.

title: Proverbs 26:2
text: As the sparrow in her wandering, as the swallow in her flying, So the curse that is causeless alighteth not.

title: Proverbs 26:3
text: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, And a rod for the back of fools.

title: Proverbs 26:4
text: Answer not a fool according to his folly, Lest thou also be like unto him.

title: Proverbs 26:5
text: Answer a fool according to his folly, Lest he be wise in his own conceit.

title: Proverbs 26:6
text: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool Cutteth off [his own] feet, [and] drinketh in damage.

title: Proverbs 26:7
text: The legs of the lame hang loose: So is a parable in the mouth of fools.

title: Proverbs 26:8
text: As one that bindeth a stone in a sling, So is he that giveth honor to a fool.

title: Proverbs 26:9
text: [ As] a thorn that goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, So is a parable in the mouth of fools.

title: Proverbs 26:10
text: [As] an archer that woundeth all, So is he that hireth a fool and he that hireth them that pass by.

title: Proverbs 26:11
text: As a dog that returneth to his vomit, [So is] a fool that repeateth his folly.

title: Proverbs 26:12
text: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? There is more hope of a fool than of him.

title: Proverbs 26:13
text: The sluggard saith, There is a lion in the way; A lion is in the streets.

title: Proverbs 26:14
text: [ As] the door turneth upon its hinges, So doth the sluggard upon his bed.

title: Proverbs 26:15
text: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish; It wearieth him to bring it again to his mouth.

title: Proverbs 26:16
text: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit Than seven men that can render a reason.

title: Proverbs 26:17
text: He that passeth by, [and] vexeth himself with strife belonging not to him, Is [like] one that taketh a dog by the ears.

title: Proverbs 26:18
text: As a madman who casteth firebrands, Arrows, and death,

title: Proverbs 26:19
text: So is the man that deceiveth his neighbor, And saith, Am not I in sport?

title: Proverbs 26:20
text: For lack of wood the fire goeth out; And where there is no whisperer, contention ceaseth.

title: Proverbs 26:21
text: [ As] coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, So is a contentious man to inflame strife.

title: Proverbs 26:22
text: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, And they go down into the innermost parts.

title: Proverbs 26:23
text: Fervent lips and a wicked heart Are [like] an earthen vessel overlaid with silver dross.

title: Proverbs 26:24
text: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips; But he layeth up deceit within him:

title: Proverbs 26:25
text: When he speaketh fair, believe him not; For there are seven abominations in his heart:

title: Proverbs 26:26
text: Though [his] hatred cover itself with guile, His wickedness shall be openly showed before the assembly.

title: Proverbs 26:27
text: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein; And he that rolleth a stone, it shall return upon him.

title: Proverbs 26:28
text: A lying tongue hateth those whom it hath wounded; And a flattering mouth worketh ruin.

title: Proverbs 27:1
text: Boast not thyself of to-morrow; For thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

title: Proverbs 27:2
text: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; A stranger, and not thine own lips.

title: Proverbs 27:3
text: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; But a fool's vexation is heavier than they both.

title: Proverbs 27:4
text: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; But who is able to stand before jealousy?

title: Proverbs 27:5
text: Better is open rebuke Than love that is hidden.

title: Proverbs 27:6
text: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; But the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

title: Proverbs 27:7
text: The full soul loatheth a honeycomb; But to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.

title: Proverbs 27:8
text: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, So is a man that wandereth from his place.

title: Proverbs 27:9
text: Oil and perfume rejoice the heart; So doth the sweetness of a man's friend [that cometh] of hearty counsel.

title: Proverbs 27:10
text: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; And go not to thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: Better is a neighbor that is near than a brother far off.

title: Proverbs 27:11
text: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, That I may answer him that reproacheth me.

title: Proverbs 27:12
text: A prudent man seeth the evil, [and] hideth himself; [But] the simple pass on, [and] suffer for it.

title: Proverbs 27:13
text: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge [that is surety] for a foreign woman.

title: Proverbs 27:14
text: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, It shall be counted a curse to him.

title: Proverbs 27:15
text: A continual dropping in a very rainy day And a contentious woman are alike:

title: Proverbs 27:16
text: He that would restrain her restraineth the wind; And his right hand encountereth oil.

title: Proverbs 27:17
text: Iron sharpeneth iron; So a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

title: Proverbs 27:18
text: Whoso keepeth the fig-tree shall eat the fruit thereof; And he that regardeth his master shall be honored.

title: Proverbs 27:19
text: As in water face [answereth] to face, So the heart of man to man.

title: Proverbs 27:20
text: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; And the eyes of man are never satisfied.

title: Proverbs 27:21
text: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; And a man is [tried] by his praise.

title: Proverbs 27:22
text: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with bruised grain, Yet will not his foolishness depart from him.

title: Proverbs 27:23
text: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, [And] look well to thy herds:

title: Proverbs 27:24
text: For riches are not for ever: And doth the crown endure unto all generations?

title: Proverbs 27:25
text: The hay is carried, and the tender grass showeth itself, And the herbs of the mountains are gathered in.

title: Proverbs 27:26
text: The lambs are for thy clothing, And the goats are the price of the field;

title: Proverbs 27:27
text: And [there will be] goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, And maintenance for thy maidens.

title: Proverbs 28:1
text: The wicked flee when no man pursueth; But the righteous are bold as a lion.

title: Proverbs 28:2
text: For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof; But by men of understanding [and] knowledge the state [thereof] shall be prolonged.

title: Proverbs 28:3
text: A needy man that oppresseth the poor Is [like] a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.

title: Proverbs 28:4
text: They that forsake the law praise the wicked; But such as keep the law contend with them.

title: Proverbs 28:5
text: Evil men understand not justice; But they that seek Jehovah understand all things.

title: Proverbs 28:6
text: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity, Than he that is perverse in [his] ways, though he be rich.

title: Proverbs 28:7
text: Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son; But he that is a companion of gluttons shameth his father.

title: Proverbs 28:8
text: He that augmenteth his substance by interest and increase, Gathereth it for him that hath pity on the poor.

title: Proverbs 28:9
text: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, Even his prayer is an abomination.

title: Proverbs 28:10
text: Whoso causeth the upright to go astray in an evil way, He shall fall himself into his own pit; But the perfect shall inherit good.

title: Proverbs 28:11
text: The rich man is wise in his own conceit; But the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.

title: Proverbs 28:12
text: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; But when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.

title: Proverbs 28:13
text: He that covereth his transgressions shall not prosper: But whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall obtain mercy.

title: Proverbs 28:14
text: Happy is the man that feareth alway; But he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.

title: Proverbs 28:15
text: [ As] a roaring lion, and a ranging bear, [So is] a wicked ruler over a poor people.

title: Proverbs 28:16
text: The prince that lacketh understanding is also a great oppressor; [But] he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.

title: Proverbs 28:17
text: A man that is laden with the blood of any person Shall flee unto the pit; Let no man stay him.

title: Proverbs 28:18
text: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be delivered; But he that is perverse in [his] ways shall fall at once.

title: Proverbs 28:19
text: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread; But he that followeth after vain [persons] shall have poverty enough.

title: Proverbs 28:20
text: A faithful man shall abound with blessings; But he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be unpunished.

title: Proverbs 28:21
text: To have respect of persons is not good; Neither that a man should transgress for a piece of bread.

title: Proverbs 28:22
text: he that hath an evil eye hasteth after riches, And knoweth not that want shall come upon him.

title: Proverbs 28:23
text: He that rebuketh a man shall afterward find more favor Than he that flattereth with the tongue.

title: Proverbs 28:24
text: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression, The same is the companion of a destroyer.

title: Proverbs 28:25
text: He that is of a greedy spirit stirreth up strife; But he that putteth his trust in Jehovah shall be made fat.

title: Proverbs 28:26
text: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool; But whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.

title: Proverbs 28:27
text: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack; But he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.

title: Proverbs 28:28
text: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; But when they perish, the righteous increase.

title: Proverbs 29:1
text: He that being often reproved hardeneth his neck Shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.

title: Proverbs 29:2
text: When the righteous are increased, the people rejoice; But when a wicked man beareth rule, the people sigh.

title: Proverbs 29:3
text: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father; But he that keepeth company with harlots wasteth [his] substance.

title: Proverbs 29:4
text: The king by justice establisheth the land; But he that exacteth gifts overthroweth it.

title: Proverbs 29:5
text: A man that flattereth his neighbor Spreadeth a net for his steps.

title: Proverbs 29:6
text: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare; But the righteous doth sing and rejoice.

title: Proverbs 29:7
text: The righteous taketh knowledge of the cause of the poor; The wicked hath not understanding to know [it] .

title: Proverbs 29:8
text: Scoffers set a city in a flame; But wise men turn away wrath.

title: Proverbs 29:9
text: If a wise man hath a controversy with a foolish man, Whether he be angry or laugh, there will be no rest.

title: Proverbs 29:10
text: The bloodthirsty hate him that is perfect; And as for the upright, they seek his life.

title: Proverbs 29:11
text: A fool uttereth all his anger; But a wise man keepeth it back and stilleth it.

title: Proverbs 29:12
text: If a ruler hearkeneth to falsehood, All his servants are wicked.

title: Proverbs 29:13
text: The poor man and the oppressor meet together; Jehovah lighteneth the eyes of them both.

title: Proverbs 29:14
text: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, His throne shall be established for ever.

title: Proverbs 29:15
text: The rod and reproof give wisdom; But a child left to himself causeth shame to his mother.

title: Proverbs 29:16
text: When the wicked are increased, transgression increaseth; But the righteous shall look upon their fall.

title: Proverbs 29:17
text: Correct thy son, and he will give thee rest; Yea, he will give delight unto thy soul.

title: Proverbs 29:18
text: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; But he that keepeth the law, happy is he.

title: Proverbs 29:19
text: A servant will not be corrected by words; For though he understand, he will not give heed.

title: Proverbs 29:20
text: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? There is more hope of a fool than of him.

title: Proverbs 29:21
text: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child Shall have him become a son at the last.

title: Proverbs 29:22
text: An angry man stirreth up strife, And a wrathful man aboundeth in transgression.

title: Proverbs 29:23
text: A man's pride shall bring him low; But he that is of a lowly spirit shall obtain honor.

title: Proverbs 29:24
text: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul; He heareth the adjuration and uttereth nothing.

title: Proverbs 29:25
text: The fear of man bringeth a snare; But whoso putteth his trust in Jehovah shall be safe.

title: Proverbs 29:26
text: Many seek the ruler's favor; But a man's judgment [cometh] from Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 29:27
text: An unjust man is an abomination to the righteous; And he that is upright in the way is an abomination to the wicked.

title: Proverbs 30:1
text: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh; The oracle. The man saith unto Ithiel, unto Ithiel and Ucal:

title: Proverbs 30:2
text: Surely I am more brutish than any man, And have not the understanding of a man;

title: Proverbs 30:3
text: And I have not learned wisdom, Neither have I the knowledge of the Holy One.

title: Proverbs 30:4
text: Who hath ascended up into heaven, and descended? Who hath gathered the wind in his fists? Who hath bound the waters in his garment? Who hath established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son's name, if thou knowest?

title: Proverbs 30:5
text: Every word of God is tried: He is a shield unto them that take refuge in him.

title: Proverbs 30:6
text: Add thou not unto his words, Lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.

title: Proverbs 30:7
text: Two things have I asked of thee; Deny me [them] not before I die:

title: Proverbs 30:8
text: Remove far from me falsehood and lies; Give me neither poverty nor riches; Feed me with the food that is needful for me:

title: Proverbs 30:9
text: Lest I be full, and deny [thee], and say, Who is Jehovah? Or lest I be poor, and steal, And use profanely the name of my God.

title: Proverbs 30:10
text: Slander not a servant unto his master, Lest he curse thee, and thou be held guilty.

title: Proverbs 30:11
text: There is a generation that curse their father, And bless not their mother.

title: Proverbs 30:12
text: There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, And [yet] are not washed from their filthiness.

title: Proverbs 30:13
text: There is a generation, oh how lofty are their eyes! And their eyelids are lifted up.

title: Proverbs 30:14
text: There is a generation whose teeth are [as] swords, and their jaw teeth [as] knives, To devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men.

title: Proverbs 30:15
text: The horseleach hath two daughters, [crying], Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, [Yea], four that say not, Enough:

title: Proverbs 30:16
text: Sheol; And the barren womb; The earth that is not satisfied with water; And the fire that saith not, Enough.

title: Proverbs 30:17
text: The eye that mocketh at his father, And despiseth to obey his mother, The ravens of the valley shall pick it out, And the young eagles shall eat it.

title: Proverbs 30:18
text: There are three things which are too wonderful for me, Yea, four which I know not:

title: Proverbs 30:19
text: The way of an eagle in the air; The way of a serpent upon a rock; The way of a ship in the midst of the sea; And the way of a man with a maiden.

title: Proverbs 30:20
text: So is the way of an adulterous woman; She eateth, and wipeth her mouth, And saith, I have done no wickedness.

title: Proverbs 30:21
text: For three things the earth doth tremble, And for four, [which] it cannot bear:

title: Proverbs 30:22
text: For a servant when he is king; And a fool when he is filled with food;

title: Proverbs 30:23
text: For an odious woman when she is married; And a handmaid that is heir to her mistress.

title: Proverbs 30:24
text: There are four things which are little upon the earth, But they are exceeding wise:

title: Proverbs 30:25
text: The ants are a people not strong, Yet they provide their food in the summer;

title: Proverbs 30:26
text: The conies are but a feeble folk, Yet make they their houses in the rocks;

title: Proverbs 30:27
text: The locusts have no king, Yet go they forth all of them by bands;

title: Proverbs 30:28
text: The lizard taketh hold with her hands, Yet is she in kings' palaces.

title: Proverbs 30:29
text: There are three things which are stately in their march, Yea, four which are stately in going:

title: Proverbs 30:30
text: The lion, which is mightiest among beasts, And turneth not away for any;

title: Proverbs 30:31
text: The greyhound; The he-goat also; And the king against whom there is no rising up.

title: Proverbs 30:32
text: If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, Or if thou hast thought evil, [Lay] thy hand upon thy mouth.

title: Proverbs 30:33
text: For the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, And the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood; So the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.

title: Proverbs 31:1
text: The words of king Lemuel; the oracle which his mother taught him.

title: Proverbs 31:2
text: What, my son? and what, O son of my womb? And what, O son of my vows?

title: Proverbs 31:3
text: Give not thy strength unto women, Nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings.

title: Proverbs 31:4
text: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; Nor for princes [to say], Where is strong drink?

title: Proverbs 31:5
text: Lest they drink, and forget the law, And pervert the justice [due] to any that is afflicted.

title: Proverbs 31:6
text: Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, And wine unto the bitter in soul:

title: Proverbs 31:7
text: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, And remember his misery no more.

title: Proverbs 31:8
text: Open thy mouth for the dumb, In the cause of all such as are left desolate.

title: Proverbs 31:9
text: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, And minister justice to the poor and needy.

title: Proverbs 31:10
text: A worthy woman who can find? For her price is far above rubies.

title: Proverbs 31:11
text: The heart of her husband trusteth in her, And he shall have no lack of gain.

title: Proverbs 31:12
text: She doeth him good and not evil All the days of her life.

title: Proverbs 31:13
text: She seeketh wool and flax, And worketh willingly with her hands.

title: Proverbs 31:14
text: She is like the merchant-ships; She bringeth her bread from afar.

title: Proverbs 31:15
text: She riseth also while it is yet night, And giveth food to her household, And their task to her maidens.

title: Proverbs 31:16
text: She considereth a field, and buyeth it; With the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.

title: Proverbs 31:17
text: She girdeth her loins with strength, And maketh strong her arms.

title: Proverbs 31:18
text: She perceiveth that her merchandise is profitable: Her lamp goeth not out by night.

title: Proverbs 31:19
text: She layeth her hands to the distaff, And her hands hold the spindle.

title: Proverbs 31:20
text: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; Yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.

title: Proverbs 31:21
text: She is not afraid of the snow for her household; For all her household are clothed with scarlet.

title: Proverbs 31:22
text: She maketh for herself carpets of tapestry; Her clothing is fine linen and purple.

title: Proverbs 31:23
text: Her husband is known in the gates, When he sitteth among the elders of the land.

title: Proverbs 31:24
text: She maketh linen garments and selleth them, And delivereth girdles unto the merchant.

title: Proverbs 31:25
text: Strength and dignity are her clothing; And she laugheth at the time to come.

title: Proverbs 31:26
text: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; And the law of kindness is on her tongue.

title: Proverbs 31:27
text: She looketh well to the ways of her household, And eateth not the bread of idleness.

title: Proverbs 31:28
text: Her children rise up, and call her blessed; Her husband [also], and he praiseth her, [saying] :

title: Proverbs 31:29
text: Many daughters have done worthily, But thou excellest them all.

title: Proverbs 31:30
text: Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; [But] a woman that feareth Jehovah, she shall be praised.

title: Proverbs 31:31
text: Give her of the fruit of her hands; And let her works praise her in the gates.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:1
text: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:2
text: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher; vanity of vanities, all is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:3
text: What profit hath man of all his labor wherein he laboreth under the sun?

title: Ecclesiastes 1:4
text: One generation goeth, and another generation cometh; but the earth abideth for ever.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:5
text: The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to its place where it ariseth.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:6
text: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it turneth about continually in its course, and the wind returneth again to its circuits.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:7
text: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full; unto the place whither the rivers go, thither they go again.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:8
text: All things are full of weariness; man cannot utter [it] : the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:9
text: That which hath been is that which shall be; and that which hath been done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:10
text: Is there a thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been long ago, in the ages which were before us.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:11
text: There is no remembrance of the former [generations] ; neither shall there be any remembrance of the latter [generations] that are to come, among those that shall come after.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:12
text: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:13
text: And I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under heaven: it is a sore travail that God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised therewith.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:14
text: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and a striving after wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:15
text: That which is crooked cannot be made straight; and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:16
text: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I have gotten me great wisdom above all that were before me in Jerusalem; yea, my heart hath had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:17
text: And I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also was a striving after wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:18
text: For in much wisdom is much grief; and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:1
text: I said in my heart, Come now, I will prove thee with mirth; therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also was vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:2
text: I said of laughter, It is mad; and of mirth, What doeth it?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:3
text: I searched in my heart how to cheer my flesh with wine, my heart yet guiding [me] with wisdom, and how to lay hold on folly, till I might see what it was good for the sons of men that they should do under heaven all the days of their life.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:4
text: I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards;

title: Ecclesiastes 2:5
text: I made me gardens and parks, and I planted trees in them of all kinds of fruit;

title: Ecclesiastes 2:6
text: I made me pools of water, to water therefrom the forest where trees were reared;

title: Ecclesiastes 2:7
text: I bought men-servants and maid-servants, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of herds and flocks, above all that were before me in Jerusalem;

title: Ecclesiastes 2:8
text: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces; I gat me men-singers and women-singers, and the delights of the sons of men, musical instruments, and that of all sorts.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:9
text: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:10
text: And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them; I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced because of all my labor; and this was my portion from all my labor.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:11
text: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labor that I had labored to do; and, behold, all was vanity and a striving after wind, and there was no profit under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:12
text: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what [can] the man [do] that cometh after the king? [even] that which hath been done long ago.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:13
text: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:14
text: The wise man's eyes are in his head, and the fool walketh in darkness: and yet I perceived that one event happeneth to them all.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:15
text: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so will it happen even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then said I in my heart, that this also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:16
text: For of the wise man, even as of the fool, there is no remembrance for ever; seeing that in the days to come all will have been long forgotten. And how doth the wise man die even as the fool!

title: Ecclesiastes 2:17
text: So I hated life, because the work that is wrought under the sun was grievous unto me; for all is vanity and a striving after wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:18
text: And I hated all my labor wherein I labored under the sun, seeing that I must leave it unto the man that shall be after me.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:19
text: And who knoweth whether he will be a wise man or a fool? yet will he have rule over all my labor wherein I have labored, and wherein I have showed myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:20
text: Therefore I turned about to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labor wherein I had labored under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:21
text: For there is a man whose labor is with wisdom, and with knowledge, and with skilfulness; yet to a man that hath not labored therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:22
text: For what hath a man of all his labor, and of the striving of his heart, wherein he laboreth under the sun?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:23
text: For all his days are [but] sorrows, and his travail is grief; yea, even in the night his heart taketh no rest. This also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:24
text: There is nothing better for a man [than] that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:25
text: For who can eat, or who can have enjoyment, more than I?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:26
text: For to the man that pleaseth him [God] giveth wisdom, and knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that pleaseth God. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:1
text: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:

title: Ecclesiastes 3:2
text: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:3
text: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:4
text: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:5
text: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:6
text: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:7
text: a time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:8
text: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:9
text: What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboreth?

title: Ecclesiastes 3:10
text: I have seen the travail which God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised therewith.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:11
text: He hath made everything beautiful in its time: also he hath set eternity in their heart, yet so that man cannot find out the work that God hath done from the beginning even to the end.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:12
text: I know that there is nothing better for them, than to rejoice, and to do good so long as they live.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:13
text: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labor, is the gift of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:14
text: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor anything taken from it; and God hath done it, that men should fear before him.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:15
text: That which is hath been long ago; and that which is to be hath long ago been: and God seeketh again that which is passed away.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:16
text: And moreover I saw under the sun, in the place of justice, that wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, that wickedness was there.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:17
text: I said in my heart, God will judge the righteous and the wicked; for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:18
text: I said in my heart, [It is] because of the sons of men, that God may prove them, and that they may see that they themselves are [but as] beasts.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:19
text: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; and man hath no preeminence above the beasts: for all is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:20
text: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:21
text: Who knoweth the spirit of man, whether it goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast, whether it goeth downward to the earth?

title: Ecclesiastes 3:22
text: Wherefore I saw that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his works; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him [back] to see what shall be after him?

title: Ecclesiastes 4:1
text: Then I returned and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and, behold, the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:2
text: Wherefore I praised the dead that have been long dead more than the living that are yet alive;

title: Ecclesiastes 4:3
text: yea, better than them both [did I esteem] him that hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:4
text: Then I saw all labor and every skilful work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbor. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:5
text: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:6
text: Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labor and striving after wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:7
text: Then I returned and saw vanity under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:8
text: There is one that is alone, and he hath not a second; yea, he hath neither son nor brother; yet is there no end of all his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied with riches. For whom then, [saith he], do I labor, and deprive my soul of good? This also is vanity, yea, it is a sore travail.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:9
text: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:10
text: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him that is alone when he falleth, and hath not another to lift him up.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:11
text: Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one be warm [alone] ?

title: Ecclesiastes 4:12
text: And if a man prevail against him that is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:13
text: Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king, who knoweth not how to receive admonition any more.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:14
text: For out of prison he came forth to be king; yea, even in his kingdom he was born poor.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:15
text: I saw all the living that walk under the sun, that they were with the youth, the second, that stood up in his stead.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:16
text: There was no end of all the people, even of all them over whom he was: yet they that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a striving after wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:1
text: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God; for to draw nigh to hear is better than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they know not that they do evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:2
text: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:3
text: For a dream cometh with a multitude of business, and a fool's voice with a multitude of words.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:4
text: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou vowest.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:5
text: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:6
text: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thy hands?

title: Ecclesiastes 5:7
text: For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, and in many words: but fear thou God.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:8
text: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a province, marvel not at the matter: for one higher than the high regardeth; and there are higher than they.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:9
text: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king [himself] is served by the field.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:10
text: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance, with increase: this also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:11
text: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them; and what advantage is there to the owner thereof, save the beholding [of them] with his eyes?

title: Ecclesiastes 5:12
text: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much; but the fulness of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:13
text: There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun, [namely], riches kept by the owner thereof to his hurt:

title: Ecclesiastes 5:14
text: and those riches perish by evil adventure; and if he hath begotten a son, there is nothing in his hand.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:15
text: As he came forth from his mother's womb, naked shall he go again as he came, and shall take nothing for his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:16
text: And this also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that he laboreth for the wind?

title: Ecclesiastes 5:17
text: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and he is sore vexed, and hath sickness and wrath.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:18
text: Behold, that which I have seen to be good and to be comely is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, wherein he laboreth under the sun, all the days of his life which God hath given him: for this is his portion.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:19
text: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor--this is the gift of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:20
text: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth [him] in the joy of his heart.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:1
text: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy upon men:

title: Ecclesiastes 6:2
text: a man to whom God giveth riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacketh nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but an alien eateth it; this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:3
text: If a man beget a hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul be not filled with good, and moreover he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he:

title: Ecclesiastes 6:4
text: for it cometh in vanity, and departeth in darkness, and the name thereof is covered with darkness;

title: Ecclesiastes 6:5
text: moreover it hath not seen the sun nor known it; this hath rest rather than the other:

title: Ecclesiastes 6:6
text: yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, and yet enjoy no good, do not all go to one place?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:7
text: All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:8
text: For what advantage hath the wise more than the fool? [or] what hath the poor man, that knoweth how to walk before the living?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:9
text: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this also is vanity and a striving after wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:10
text: Whatsoever hath been, the name thereof was given long ago; and it is known what man is; neither can he contend with him that is mightier than he.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:11
text: Seeing there are many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:12
text: For who knoweth what is good for man in [his] life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:1
text: A [good] name is better than precious oil; and the day of death, than the day of one's birth.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:2
text: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:3
text: Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made glad.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:4
text: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:5
text: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:6
text: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:7
text: Surely extortion maketh the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroyeth the understanding.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:8
text: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof; [and] the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:9
text: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry; for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:10
text: Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not inquire wisely concerning this.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:11
text: Wisdom is as good as an inheritance; yea, more excellent is it for them that see the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:12
text: For wisdom is a defence, even as money is a defence; but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom preserveth the life of him that hath it.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:13
text: Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:14
text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yea, God hath made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man should not find out anything [that shall be] after him.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:15
text: All this have I seen in my days of vanity: there is a righteous man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth [his life] in his evil-doing.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:16
text: Be not righteous overmuch; neither make thyself overwise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:17
text: Be not overmuch wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:18
text: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from that withdraw not thy hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth from them all.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:19
text: Wisdom is a strength to the wise man more than ten rulers that are in a city.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:20
text: Surely there is not a righteous man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:21
text: Also take not heed unto all words that are spoken, lest thou hear thy servant curse thee;

title: Ecclesiastes 7:22
text: for oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:23
text: All this have I proved in wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:24
text: That which is, is far off and exceeding deep; who can find it out?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:25
