text: I turned about, and my heart [was set] to know and to search out, and to seek wisdom and the reason [of things], and to know that wickedness is folly, and that foolishness is madness.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:26
text: And I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, [and] whose hands are bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her. [

title: Ecclesiastes 7:27
text: Behold, this have I found, saith the Preacher, [laying] one thing to another, to find out the account;

title: Ecclesiastes 7:28
text: which my soul still seeketh, but I have not found: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:29
text: Behold, this only have I found: that God made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:1
text: Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? A man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:2
text: I [counsel thee], Keep the king's command, and that in regard of the oath of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:3
text: Be not hasty to go out of his presence; persist not in an evil thing: for he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:4
text: For the king's word [hath] power; and who may say unto him, What doest thou?

title: Ecclesiastes 8:5
text: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall know no evil thing; and a wise man's heart discerneth time and judgment:

title: Ecclesiastes 8:6
text: for to every purpose there is a time and judgment; because the misery of man is great upon him:

title: Ecclesiastes 8:7
text: for he knoweth not that which shall be; for who can tell him how it shall be?

title: Ecclesiastes 8:8
text: There is no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither hath he power over the day of death; and there is no discharge in war: neither shall wickedness deliver him that is given to it.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:9
text: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: [there is] a time wherein one man hath power over another to his hurt.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:10
text: So I saw the wicked buried, and they came [to the grave] ; and they that had done right went away from the holy place, and were forgotten in the city: this also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:11
text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:12
text: Though a sinner do evil a hundred times, and prolong his [days], yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, that fear before him:

title: Ecclesiastes 8:13
text: but it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong [his] days, [which are] as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:14
text: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth, that there are righteous men unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there are wicked men to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:15
text: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be joyful: for that shall abide with him in his labor [all] the days of his life which God hath given him under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:16
text: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth (for also there is that neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes), [

title: Ecclesiastes 8:17
text: then I beheld all the work of God, that man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because however much a man labor to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yea moreover, though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:1
text: For all this I laid to my heart, even to explore all this: that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God; whether it be love or hatred, man knoweth it not; all is before them.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:2
text: All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth and to him that sacrificeth not; as is the good, so is the sinner; [and] he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:3
text: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event unto all: yea also, the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that [they go] to the dead.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:4
text: For to him that is joined with all the living there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:5
text: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not anything, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:6
text: As well their love, as their hatred and their envy, is perished long ago; neither have they any more a portion for ever in anything that is done under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:7
text: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God hath already accepted thy works.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:8
text: Let thy garments be always white; and let not thy head lack oil.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:9
text: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of thy life of vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all thy days of vanity: for that is thy portion in life, and in thy labor wherein thou laborest under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:10
text: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do [it] with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, whither thou goest.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:11
text: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:12
text: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare, even so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:13
text: I have also seen wisdom under the sun on this wise, and it seemed great unto me:

title: Ecclesiastes 9:14
text: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:15
text: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:16
text: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:17
text: The words of the wise heard in quiet are better than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:18
text: Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroyeth much good.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:1
text: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to send forth an evil odor; [so] doth a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:2
text: A wise man's heart is at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:3
text: Yea also, when the fool walketh by the way, his understanding faileth him, and he saith to every one [that] he is a fool.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:4
text: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for gentleness allayeth great offences.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:5
text: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as it were an error which proceedeth from the ruler:

title: Ecclesiastes 10:6
text: folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:7
text: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking like servants upon the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:8
text: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh through a wall, a serpent shall bite him.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:9
text: Whoso heweth out stones shall be hurt therewith; [and] he that cleaveth wood is endangered thereby.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:10
text: If the iron be blunt, and one do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:11
text: If the serpent bite before it is charmed, then is there no advantage in the charmer.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:12
text: The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:13
text: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:14
text: A fool also multiplieth words: [yet] man knoweth not what shall be; and that which shall be after him, who can tell him?

title: Ecclesiastes 10:15
text: The labor of fools wearieth every one of them; for he knoweth not how to go to the city.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:16
text: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!

title: Ecclesiastes 10:17
text: Happy art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

title: Ecclesiastes 10:18
text: By slothfulness the roof sinketh in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaketh.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:19
text: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh glad the life; and money answereth all things.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:20
text: Revile not the king, no, not in thy thought; and revile not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:1
text: Cast thy bread upon the waters; for thou shalt find it after many days.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:2
text: Give a portion to seven, yea, even unto eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:3
text: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth; and if a tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there shall it be.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:4
text: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:5
text: As thou knowest not what is the way of the wind, [nor] how the bones [do grow] in the womb of her that is with child; even so thou knowest not the work of God who doeth all.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:6
text: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thy hand; for thou knowest not which shall prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:7
text: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:8
text: Yea, if a man live many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:9
text: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth, and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart, and in the sight of thine eyes; but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:10
text: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh; for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:1
text: Remember also thy Creator in the days of thy youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:2
text: before the sun, and the light, and the moon, and the stars, are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:3
text: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows shall be darkened,

title: Ecclesiastes 12:4
text: and the doors shall be shut in the street; when the sound of the grinding is low, and one shall rise up at the voice of a bird, and all the daughters of music shall be brought low;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:5
text: yea, they shall be afraid of [that which is] high, and terrors [shall be] in the way; and the almond-tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail; because man goeth to his everlasting home, and the mourners go about the streets:

title: Ecclesiastes 12:6
text: before the silver cord is loosed, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern,

title: Ecclesiastes 12:7
text: and the dust returneth to the earth as it was, and the spirit returneth unto God who gave it.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:8
text: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher; all is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:9
text: And further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he pondered, and sought out, [and] set in order many proverbs.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:10
text: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words, and that which was written uprightly, [even] words of truth.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:11
text: The words of the wise are as goads; and as nails well fastened are [the words of] the masters of assemblies, [which] are given from one shepherd.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:12
text: And furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:13
text: [This is] the end of the matter; all hath been heard: fear God, and keep his commandments; for this is the whole [duty] of man.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:14
text: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.

title: Song of Solomon 1:1
text: The Song of songs, which is Solomon's.

title: Song of Solomon 1:2
text: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; For thy love is better than wine.

title: Song of Solomon 1:3
text: Thine oils have a goodly fragrance; Thy name is [as] oil poured forth; Therefore do the virgins love thee.

title: Song of Solomon 1:4
text: Draw me; we will run after thee: The king hath brought me into his chambers; We will be glad and rejoice in thee; We will make mention of thy love more than of wine: Rightly do they love thee. [

title: Song of Solomon 1:5
text: I am black, but comely, Oh ye daughters of Jerusalem, As the tents of Kedar, As the curtains of Solomon.

title: Song of Solomon 1:6
text: Look not upon me, because I am swarthy, Because the sun hath scorched me. My mother's sons were incensed against me; They made me keeper of the vineyards; [But] mine own vineyard have I not kept.

title: Song of Solomon 1:7
text: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, Where thou feedest [thy flock], Where thou makest [it] to rest at noon: For why should I be as one that is veiled Beside the flocks of thy companions?

title: Song of Solomon 1:8
text: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, Go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, And feed thy kids beside the shepherds' tents.

title: Song of Solomon 1:9
text: I have compared thee, O my love, To a steed in Pharaoh's chariots.

title: Song of Solomon 1:10
text: Thy cheeks are comely with plaits [of hair], Thy neck with strings of jewels.

title: Song of Solomon 1:11
text: We will make thee plaits of gold With studs of silver.

title: Song of Solomon 1:12
text: While the king sat at his table, My spikenard sent forth its fragrance.

title: Song of Solomon 1:13
text: My beloved is unto me [as] a bundle of myrrh, That lieth betwixt my breasts.

title: Song of Solomon 1:14
text: My beloved is unto me [as] a cluster of henna-flowers In the vineyards of En-gedi.

title: Song of Solomon 1:15
text: Behold, thou art fair, my love; Behold thou art fair; Thine eyes are [as] doves.

title: Song of Solomon 1:16
text: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: Also our couch is green.

title: Song of Solomon 1:17
text: The beams of our house are cedars, [And] our rafters are firs.

title: Song of Solomon 2:1
text: I am a rose of Sharon, A lily of the valleys.

title: Song of Solomon 2:2
text: As a lily among thorns, So is my love among the daughters.

title: Song of Solomon 2:3
text: As the apple-tree among the trees of the wood, So is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, And his fruit was sweet to my taste.

title: Song of Solomon 2:4
text: He brought me to the banqueting-house, And his banner over me was love.

title: Song of Solomon 2:5
text: Stay ye me with raisins, refresh me with apples; For I am sick from love.

title: Song of Solomon 2:6
text: His left hand [is] under my head, And his right hand doth embrace me.

title: Song of Solomon 2:7
text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake [my] love, Until he please.

title: Song of Solomon 2:8
text: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh, Leaping upon the mountains, Skipping upon the hills.

title: Song of Solomon 2:9
text: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: Behold, he standeth behind our wall; He looketh in at the windows; He glanceth through the lattice.

title: Song of Solomon 2:10
text: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

title: Song of Solomon 2:11
text: For, lo, the winter is past; The rain is over and gone;

title: Song of Solomon 2:12
text: The flowers appear on the earth; The time of the singing [of birds] is come, And the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land;

title: Song of Solomon 2:13
text: The fig-tree ripeneth her green figs, And the vines are in blossom; They give forth their fragrance. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.

title: Song of Solomon 2:14
text: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, In the covert of the steep place, Let me see thy countenance, Let me hear thy voice; For sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.

title: Song of Solomon 2:15
text: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, That spoil the vineyards; For our vineyards are in blossom.

title: Song of Solomon 2:16
text: My beloved is mine, and I am his: He feedeth [his flock] among the lilies.

title: Song of Solomon 2:17
text: Until the day be cool, and the shadows flee away, Turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart Upon the mountains of Bether.

title: Song of Solomon 3:1
text: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

title: Song of Solomon 3:2
text: [ I said], I will rise now, and go about the city; In the streets and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

title: Song of Solomon 3:3
text: The watchmen that go about the city found me; [To whom I said], Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?

title: Song of Solomon 3:4
text: It was but a little that I passed from them, When I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, Until I had brought him into my mother's house, And into the chamber of her that conceived me.

title: Song of Solomon 3:5
text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake [my] love, Until he please.

title: Song of Solomon 3:6
text: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness Like pillars of smoke, Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, With all powders of the merchant?

title: Song of Solomon 3:7
text: Behold, it is the litter of Solomon; Threescore mighty men are about it, Of the mighty men of Israel.

title: Song of Solomon 3:8
text: They all handle the sword, [and] are expert in war: Every man hath his sword upon his thigh, Because of fear in the night.

title: Song of Solomon 3:9
text: King Solomon made himself a palanquin Of the wood of Lebanon.

title: Song of Solomon 3:10
text: He made the pillars thereof of silver, The bottom thereof of gold, the seat of it of purple, The midst thereof being paved with love, From the daughters of Jerusalem.

title: Song of Solomon 3:11
text: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon, With the crown wherewith his mother hath crowned him In the day of his espousals, And in the day of the gladness of his heart.

title: Song of Solomon 4:1
text: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; Thine eyes are [as] doves behind thy veil. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, That lie along the side of mount Gilead.

title: Song of Solomon 4:2
text: Thy teeth are like a flock [of ewes] that are [newly] shorn, Which are come up from the washing, Whereof every one hath twins, And none is bereaved among them.

title: Song of Solomon 4:3
text: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, And thy mouth is comely. Thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate Behind thy veil.

title: Song of Solomon 4:4
text: Thy neck is like the tower of David builded for an armory, Whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, All the shields of the mighty men.

title: Song of Solomon 4:5
text: Thy two breasts are like two fawns That are twins of a roe, Which feed among the lilies.

title: Song of Solomon 4:6
text: Until the day be cool, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, And to the hill of frankincense.

title: Song of Solomon 4:7
text: Thou art all fair, my love; And there is no spot in thee.

title: Song of Solomon 4:8
text: Come with me from Lebanon, [my] bride, With me from Lebanon: Look from the top of Amana, From the top of Senir and Hermon, From the lions' dens, From the mountains of the leopards.

title: Song of Solomon 4:9
text: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, [my] bride; Thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, With one chain of thy neck.

title: Song of Solomon 4:10
text: How fair is thy love, my sister, [my] bride! How much better is thy love than wine! And the fragrance of thine oils than all manner of spices!

title: Song of Solomon 4:11
text: Thy lips, O [my] bride, drop [as] the honeycomb: Honey and milk are under thy tongue; And the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

title: Song of Solomon 4:12
text: A garden shut up is my sister, [my] bride; A spring shut up, a fountain sealed.

title: Song of Solomon 4:13
text: Thy shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits; Henna with spikenard plants,

title: Song of Solomon 4:14
text: Spikenard and saffron, Calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; Myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices.

title: Song of Solomon 4:15
text: [ Thou art] a fountain of gardens, A well of living waters, And flowing streams from Lebanon.

title: Song of Solomon 4:16
text: Awake, O north wind; And come, thou south; Blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, And eat his precious fruits.

title: Song of Solomon 5:1
text: I am come into my garden, my sister, [my] bride: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends; Drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

title: Song of Solomon 5:2
text: I was asleep, but my heart waked: It is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, [saying], Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; For my head is filled with dew, My locks with the drops of the night.

title: Song of Solomon 5:3
text: I have put off my garment; How shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?

title: Song of Solomon 5:4
text: My beloved put in his hand by the hole [of the door], And my heart was moved for him.

title: Song of Solomon 5:5
text: I rose up to open to my beloved; And my hands dropped with myrrh, And my fingers with liquid myrrh, Upon the handles of the bolt.

title: Song of Solomon 5:6
text: I opened to my beloved; But my beloved had withdrawn himself, [and] was gone. My soul had failed me when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

title: Song of Solomon 5:7
text: The watchmen that go about the city found me, They smote me, they wounded me; The keepers of the walls took away my mantle from me.

title: Song of Solomon 5:8
text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, If ye find my beloved, That ye tell him, that I am sick from love.

title: Song of Solomon 5:9
text: What is thy beloved more than [another] beloved, O thou fairest among women? What is thy beloved more than [another] beloved, That thou dost so adjure us?

title: Song of Solomon 5:10
text: My beloved is white and ruddy, The chiefest among ten thousand.

title: Song of Solomon 5:11
text: His head is [as] the most fine gold; His locks are bushy, [and] black as a raven.

title: Song of Solomon 5:12
text: His eyes are like doves beside the water-brooks, Washed with milk, [and] fitly set.

title: Song of Solomon 5:13
text: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, [As] banks of sweet herbs: His lips are [as] lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.

title: Song of Solomon 5:14
text: His hands are [as] rings of gold set with beryl: His body is [as] ivory work overlaid [with] sapphires.

title: Song of Solomon 5:15
text: His legs are [as] pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: His aspect is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

title: Song of Solomon 5:16
text: His mouth is most sweet; Yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

title: Song of Solomon 6:1
text: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? Whither hath thy beloved turned him, That we may seek him with thee?

title: Song of Solomon 6:2
text: My beloved is gone down to his garden, To the beds of spices, To feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

title: Song of Solomon 6:3
text: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine; He feedeth [his flock] among the lilies,

title: Song of Solomon 6:4
text: Thou art fair, O my love, as Tirzah, Comely as Jerusalem, Terrible as an army with banners.

title: Song of Solomon 6:5
text: Turn away thine eyes from me, For they have overcome me. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, That lie along the side of Gilead.

title: Song of Solomon 6:6
text: Thy teeth are like a flock of ewes, Which are come up from the washing; Whereof every one hath twins, And none is bereaved among them.

title: Song of Solomon 6:7
text: Thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate Behind thy veil.

title: Song of Solomon 6:8
text: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, And virgins without number.

title: Song of Solomon 6:9
text: My dove, my undefiled, is [but] one; She is the only one of her mother; She is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and called her blessed; [Yea], the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

title: Song of Solomon 6:10
text: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, Fair as the moon, Clear as the sun, Terrible as an army with banners?

title: Song of Solomon 6:11
text: I went down into the garden of nuts, To see the green plants of the valley, To see whether the vine budded, [And] the pomegranates were in flower.

title: Song of Solomon 6:12
text: Before I was aware, my soul set me [Among] the chariots of my princely people.

title: Song of Solomon 6:13
text: Return, return, O Shulammite; Return, return, that we may look upon thee. Why will ye look upon the Shulammite, As upon the dance of Mahanaim?

title: Song of Solomon 7:1
text: How beautiful are thy feet in sandals, O prince's daughter! Thy rounded thighs are like jewels, The work of the hands of a skilful workman.

title: Song of Solomon 7:2
text: Thy body is [like] a round goblet, [Wherein] no mingled wine is wanting: Thy waist is [like] a heap of wheat Set about with lilies.

title: Song of Solomon 7:3
text: Thy two breasts are like two fawns That are twins of a roe.

title: Song of Solomon 7:4
text: Thy neck is like the tower of ivory; Thine eyes [as] the pools in Heshbon, By the gate of Bath-rabbim; Thy nose is like the tower of Lebanon Which looketh toward Damascus.

title: Song of Solomon 7:5
text: Thy head upon thee is like Carmel, And the hair of thy head like purple; The king is held captive in the tresses [thereof] .

title: Song of Solomon 7:6
text: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!

title: Song of Solomon 7:7
text: This thy stature is like to a palm-tree, And thy breasts to its clusters.

title: Song of Solomon 7:8
text: I said, I will climb up into the palm-tree, I will take hold of the branches thereof: Let thy breasts be as clusters of the vine, And the smell of thy breath like apples,

title: Song of Solomon 7:9
text: And thy mouth like the best wine, That goeth down smoothly for my beloved, Gliding through the lips of those that are asleep.

title: Song of Solomon 7:10
text: I am my beloved's; And his desire is toward me.

title: Song of Solomon 7:11
text: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; Let us lodge in the villages.

title: Song of Solomon 7:12
text: Let us get up early to the vineyards; Let us see whether the vine hath budded, [And] its blossom is open, [And] the pomegranates are in flower: There will I give thee my love.

title: Song of Solomon 7:13
text: The mandrakes give forth fragrance; And at our doors are all manner of precious fruits, new and old, Which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.

title: Song of Solomon 8:1
text: Oh that thou wert as my brother, That sucked the breasts of my mother! [When] I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; Yea, and none would despise me.

title: Song of Solomon 8:2
text: I would lead thee, [and] bring thee into my mother's house, Who would instruct me; I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine, Of the juice of my pomegranate.

title: Song of Solomon 8:3
text: His left hand [should be] under my head, And his right hand should embrace me.

title: Song of Solomon 8:4
text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, That ye stir not up, nor awake [my] love, Until he please.

title: Song of Solomon 8:5
text: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, Leaning upon her beloved? Under the apple-tree I awakened thee: There thy mother was in travail with thee, There was she in travail that brought thee forth.

title: Song of Solomon 8:6
text: Set me as a seal upon thy heart, As a seal upon thine arm: For love is strong as death; Jealousy is cruel as Sheol; The flashes thereof are flashes of fire, A very flame of Jehovah.

title: Song of Solomon 8:7
text: Many waters cannot quench love, Neither can floods drown it: If a man would give all the substance of his house for love, He would utterly be contemned.

title: Song of Solomon 8:8
text: We have a little sister, And she hath no breasts: What shall we do for our sister In the day when she shall be spoken for?

title: Song of Solomon 8:9
text: If she be a wall, We will build upon her a turret of silver: And if she be a door, We will inclose her with boards of cedar.

title: Song of Solomon 8:10
text: I am a wall, and my breasts like the towers [thereof] Then was I in his eyes as one that found peace.

title: Song of Solomon 8:11
text: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; He let out the vineyard unto keepers; Every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand [pieces] of silver.

title: Song of Solomon 8:12
text: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: Thou, O Solomon, shalt have the thousand, And those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.

title: Song of Solomon 8:13
text: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, The companions hearken for thy voice: Cause me to hear it.

title: Song of Solomon 8:14
text: Make haste, my beloved, And be thou like to a roe or to a young hart Upon the mountains of spices.

title: Isaiah 1:1
text: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

title: Isaiah 1:2
text: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth; for Jehovah hath spoken: I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.

title: Isaiah 1:3
text: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib; [but] Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.

title: Isaiah 1:4
text: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evil-doers, children that deal corruptly! they have forsaken Jehovah, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they are estranged [and gone] backward.

title: Isaiah 1:5
text: Why will ye be still stricken, that ye revolt more and more? the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.

title: Isaiah 1:6
text: From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; [but] wounds, and bruises, and fresh stripes: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with oil.

title: Isaiah 1:7
text: Your country is desolate; your cities are burned with fire; your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.

title: Isaiah 1:8
text: And the daughter of Zion is left as a booth in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.

title: Isaiah 1:9
text: Except Jehovah of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, we should have been like unto Gomorrah.

title: Isaiah 1:10
text: Hear the word of Jehovah, ye rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah.

title: Isaiah 1:11
text: What unto me is the multitude of your sacrifices? saith Jehovah: I have had enough of the burnt-offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he-goats.

title: Isaiah 1:12
text: When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this at your hand, to trample my courts?

title: Isaiah 1:13
text: Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; new moon and sabbath, the calling of assemblies,-- I cannot away with iniquity and the solemn meeting. [

title: Isaiah 1:14
text: Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth; they are a trouble unto me; I am weary of bearing them.

title: Isaiah 1:15
text: And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you; yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.

title: Isaiah 1:16
text: Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil;

title: Isaiah 1:17
text: learn to do well; seek justice, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.

title: Isaiah 1:18
text: Come now, and let us reason together, saith Jehovah: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

title: Isaiah 1:19
text: If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land:

title: Isaiah 1:20
text: but if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword; for the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken it.

title: Isaiah 1:21
text: How is the faithful city become a harlot! she that was full of justice! righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers.

title: Isaiah 1:22
text: Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water.

title: Isaiah 1:23
text: Thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves; every one loveth bribes, and followeth after rewards: they judge not the fatherless, neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them.

title: Isaiah 1:24
text: Therefore saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies;

title: Isaiah 1:25
text: and I will turn my hand upon thee, and thoroughly purge away thy dross, and will take away all thy tin;

title: Isaiah 1:26
text: and I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called The city of righteousness, a faithful town.

title: Isaiah 1:27
text: Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.

title: Isaiah 1:28
text: But the destruction of transgressors and sinners shall be together, and they that forsake Jehovah shall be consumed.

title: Isaiah 1:29
text: For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired, and ye shall be confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen.

title: Isaiah 1:30
text: For ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water.

title: Isaiah 1:31
text: And the strong shall be as tow, and his work as a spark; and they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them.

title: Isaiah 2:1
text: The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

title: Isaiah 2:2
text: And it shall come to pass in the latter days, that the mountain of Jehovah's house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.

title: Isaiah 2:3
text: And many peoples shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of Jehovah, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth [ the law, and the word of Jehovah from Jerusalem.

title: Isaiah 2:4
text: And he will judge between the nations, and will decide concerning many peoples; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning-hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

title: Isaiah 2:5
text: O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of Jehovah.

title: Isaiah 2:6
text: For thou hast forsaken thy people the house of Jacob, because they are filled [with customs] from the east, and [are] soothsayers like the Philistines, and they strike hands with the children of foreigners.

title: Isaiah 2:7
text: And their land is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures; their land also is full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots.

title: Isaiah 2:8
text: Their land also is full of idols; they worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made.

title: Isaiah 2:9
text: And the mean man is bowed down, and the great man is brought low: therefore forgive them not.

title: Isaiah 2:10
text: Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, from before the terror of Jehovah, and from the glory of his majesty.

title: Isaiah 2:11
text: The lofty looks of man shall be brought low, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and Jehovah alone shall be exalted in that day.

title: Isaiah 2:12
text: For there shall be a day of Jehovah of hosts upon all that is proud and haughty, and upon all that is lifted up; and it shall be brought low;

title: Isaiah 2:13
text: and upon all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of Bashan,

title: Isaiah 2:14
text: and upon all the high mountains, and upon all the hills that are lifted up,

title: Isaiah 2:15
text: and upon every lofty tower, and upon every fortified wall,

title: Isaiah 2:16
text: and upon all the ships of Tarshish, and upon all pleasant imagery.

title: Isaiah 2:17
text: And the loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be brought low; and Jehovah alone shall be exalted in that day.

title: Isaiah 2:18
text: And the idols shall utterly pass away.

title: Isaiah 2:19
text: And men shall go into the caves of the rocks, and into the holes of the earth, from before the terror of Jehovah, and from the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake mightily the earth. [

title: Isaiah 2:20
text: In that day men shall cast away their idols of silver, and their idols of gold, which have been made for them to worship, to the moles and to the bats;

title: Isaiah 2:21
text: to go into the caverns of the rocks, and into the clefts of the ragged rocks, from before the terror of Jehovah, and from the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake mightily the earth.

title: Isaiah 2:22
text: Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for wherein is he to be accounted of?

title: Isaiah 3:1
text: For, behold, the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, doth take away from Jerusalem and from Judah stay and staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water;

title: Isaiah 3:2
text: the mighty man, and the man of war; the judge, and the prophet, and the diviner, and the elder;

title: Isaiah 3:3
text: the captain of fifty, and the honorable man, and the counsellor, and the expert artificer, and the skilful enchanter.

title: Isaiah 3:4
text: And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them.

title: Isaiah 3:5
text: And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbor: the child shall behave himself proudly against the old man, and the base against the honorable.

title: Isaiah 3:6
text: When a man shall take hold of his brother in the house of his father, [saying], Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand;

title: Isaiah 3:7
text: in that day shall he lift up [his voice], saying, I will not be a healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing: ye shall not make me ruler of the people.

title: Isaiah 3:8
text: For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen; because their tongue and their doings are against Jehovah, to provoke the eyes of his glory.

title: Isaiah 3:9
text: The show of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have done evil unto themselves.

title: Isaiah 3:10
text: Say ye of the righteous, that [it shall be] well [with him] ; for they shall eat the fruit of their doings.

title: Isaiah 3:11
text: Woe unto the wicked! [it shall be] ill [with him] ; for what his hands have done shall be done unto him.

title: Isaiah 3:12
text: As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they that lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.

title: Isaiah 3:13
text: Jehovah standeth up to contend, and standeth to judge the peoples.

title: Isaiah 3:14
text: Jehovah will enter into judgment with the elders of his people, and the princes thereof: It is ye that have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses:

title: Isaiah 3:15
text: what mean ye that ye crush my people, and grind the face of the poor? saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts.

title: Isaiah 3:16
text: Moreover Jehovah said, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with outstretched necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet;

title: Isaiah 3:17
text: therefore the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and Jehovah will lay bare their secret parts.

title: Isaiah 3:18
text: In that day the Lord will take away the beauty of their anklets, and the cauls, and the crescents;

title: Isaiah 3:19
text: the pendants, and the bracelets, and the mufflers;

title: Isaiah 3:20
text: the headtires, and the ankle chains, and the sashes, and the perfume-boxes, and the amulets;

title: Isaiah 3:21
text: the rings, and the nose-jewels;

title: Isaiah 3:22
text: the festival robes, and the mantles, and the shawls, and the satchels;

title: Isaiah 3:23
text: the hand-mirrors, and the fine linen, and the turbans, and the veils.

title: Isaiah 3:24
text: And it shall come to pass, that instead of sweet spices there shall be rottenness; and instead of a girdle, a rope; and instead of well set hair, baldness; and instead of a robe, a girding of sackcloth; branding instead of beauty.

title: Isaiah 3:25
text: Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war.

title: Isaiah 3:26
text: And her gates shall lament and mourn; and she shall be desolate and sit upon the ground.

title: Isaiah 4:1
text: And seven women shall take hold of one man in that day, saying, We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name; take thou away our reproach.

title: Isaiah 4:2
text: In that day shall the branch of Jehovah be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel.

title: Isaiah 4:3
text: And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem;

title: Isaiah 4:4
text: when the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from the midst thereof, by the spirit of justice, and by the spirit of burning.

title: Isaiah 4:5
text: And Jehovah will create over the whole habitation of mount Zion, and over her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory [shall be spread] a covering.

title: Isaiah 4:6
text: And there shall be a pavilion for a shade in the day-time from the heat, and for a refuge and for a covert from storm and from rain.

title: Isaiah 5:1
text: Let me sing for my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My wellbeloved had a vineyard in a very fruitful hill:

title: Isaiah 5:2
text: and he digged it, and gathered out the stones thereof, and planted it with the choicest vine, and built a tower in the midst of it, and also hewed out a winepress therein: and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes.

title: Isaiah 5:3
text: And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard.

title: Isaiah 5:4
text: What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes?

title: Isaiah 5:5
text: And now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; I will break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down:

title: Isaiah 5:6
text: and I will lay it waste; it shall not be pruned nor hoed; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.

title: Isaiah 5:7
text: For the vineyard of Jehovah of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for justice, but, behold, oppression; for righteousness, but, behold, a cry.

title: Isaiah 5:8
text: Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no room, and ye be made to dwell alone in the midst of the land!

title: Isaiah 5:9
text: In mine ears [saith] Jehovah of hosts, Of a truth many houses shall be desolate, even great and fair, without inhabitant.

title: Isaiah 5:10
text: For ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield [but] an ephah.

title: Isaiah 5:11
text: Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that tarry late into the night, till wine inflame them!

title: Isaiah 5:12
text: And the harp and the lute, the tabret and the pipe, and wine, are [in] their feasts; but they regard not the work of Jehovah, neither have they considered the operation of his hands.

title: Isaiah 5:13
text: Therefore my people are gone into captivity for lack of knowledge; and their honorable men are famished, and their multitude are parched with thirst.

title: Isaiah 5:14
text: Therefore Sheol hath enlarged its desire, and opened its mouth without measure; and their glory, and their multitude, and their pomp, and he that rejoiceth among them, descend [into it] . [

title: Isaiah 5:15
text: And the mean man is bowed down, and the great man is humbled, and the eyes of the lofty are humbled:

title: Isaiah 5:16
text: but Jehovah of hosts is exalted in justice, and God the Holy One is sanctified in righteousness.

title: Isaiah 5:17
text: Then shall the lambs feed as in their pasture, and the waste places of the fat ones shall wanderers eat.

title: Isaiah 5:18
text: Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, and sin as it were with a cart rope;

title: Isaiah 5:19
text: that say, Let him make speed, let him hasten his work, that we may see it; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw nigh and come, that we may know it!

title: Isaiah 5:20
text: Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!

title: Isaiah 5:21
text: Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!

title: Isaiah 5:22
text: Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink;

title: Isaiah 5:23
text: that justify the wicked for a bribe, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him!

title: Isaiah 5:24
text: Therefore as the tongue of fire devoureth the stubble, and as the dry grass sinketh down in the flame, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust; because they have rejected the law of Jehovah of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

title: Isaiah 5:25
text: Therefore is the anger of Jehovah kindled against his people, and he hath stretched forth his hand against them, and hath smitten them; and the mountains tremble, and their dead bodies are as refuse in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

title: Isaiah 5:26
text: And he will lift up an ensign to the nations from far, and will hiss for them from the end of the earth; and, behold, they shall come with speed swiftly.

title: Isaiah 5:27
text: None shall be weary nor stumble among them; none shall slumber nor sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken:

title: Isaiah 5:28
text: whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent; their horses' hoofs shall be accounted as flint, and their wheels as a whirlwind:

title: Isaiah 5:29
text: their roaring shall be like a lioness, they shall roar like young lions; yea, they shall roar, and lay hold of the prey, and carry it away safe, and there shall be none to deliver.

title: Isaiah 5:30
text: And they shall roar against them in that day like the roaring of the sea: and if one look unto the land, behold, darkness [and] distress; and the light is darkened in the clouds thereof.

title: Isaiah 6:1
text: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.

title: Isaiah 6:2
text: Above him stood the seraphim: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.

title: Isaiah 6:3
text: And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is Jehovah of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.

title: Isaiah 6:4
text: And the foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.

title: Isaiah 6:5
text: Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, Jehovah of hosts.

title: Isaiah 6:6
text: Then flew one of the seraphim unto me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar:

title: Isaiah 6:7
text: and he touched my mouth with it, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin forgiven.

title: Isaiah 6:8
text: And I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then I said, Here am I; send me.

title: Isaiah 6:9
text: And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.

title: Isaiah 6:10
text: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn again, and be healed.

title: Isaiah 6:11
text: Then said I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until cities be waste without inhabitant, and houses without man, and the land become utterly waste,

title: Isaiah 6:12
text: and Jehovah have removed men far away, and the forsaken places be many in the midst of the land.

title: Isaiah 6:13
text: And if there be yet a tenth in it, it also shall in turn be eaten up: as a terebinth, and as an oak, whose stock remaineth, when they are felled; so the holy seed is the stock thereof.

title: Isaiah 7:1
text: And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.

title: Isaiah 7:2
text: And it was told the house of David, saying, Syria is confederate with Ephraim. And his heart trembled, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the forest tremble with the wind.

title: Isaiah 7:3
text: Then said Jehovah unto Isaiah, Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shear-jashub thy son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, in the highway of the fuller's field;

title: Isaiah 7:4
text: and say unto him, Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither let thy heart be faint, because of these two tails of smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.

title: Isaiah 7:5
text: Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have purposed evil against thee, saying,

title: Isaiah 7:6
text: Let us go up against Judah, and vex it, and let us make a breach therein for us, and set up a king in the midst of it, even the son of Tabeel;

title: Isaiah 7:7
text: thus saith the Lord Jehovah, It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.

title: Isaiah 7:8
text: For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken in pieces, so that it shall not be a people:

title: Isaiah 7:9
text: and the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah's son. If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.

title: Isaiah 7:10
text: And Jehovah spake again unto Ahaz, saying,

title: Isaiah 7:11
text: Ask thee a sign of Jehovah thy God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above.

title: Isaiah 7:12
text: But Ahaz said, I will not ask, neither will I tempt Jehovah.

title: Isaiah 7:13
text: And he said, Hear ye now, O house of David: Is it a small thing for you to weary men, that ye will weary my God also?

title: Isaiah 7:14
text: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.

title: Isaiah 7:15
text: Butter and honey shall he eat, when he knoweth to refuse the evil, and choose the good.

title: Isaiah 7:16
text: For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land whose two kings thou abhorrest shall be forsaken.

title: Isaiah 7:17
text: Jehovah will bring upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon thy father's house, days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah--[ even] the king of Assyria.

title: Isaiah 7:18
text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that Jehovah will hiss for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.

title: Isaiah 7:19
text: And they shall come, and shall rest all of them in the desolate valleys, and in the clefts of the rocks, and upon all thorn-hedges, and upon all pastures.

title: Isaiah 7:20
text: In that day will the Lord shave with a razor that is hired in the parts beyond the River, [even] with the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet; and it shall also consume the beard.

title: Isaiah 7:21
text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that a man shall keep alive a young cow, and two sheep;

title: Isaiah 7:22
text: and it shall come to pass, that because of the abundance of milk which they shall give he shall eat butter: for butter and honey shall every one eat that is left in the midst of the land.

title: Isaiah 7:23
text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that every place, where there were a thousand vines at a thousand silverlings, shall be for briers and thorns.

title: Isaiah 7:24
text: With arrows and with bow shall one come thither, because all the land shall be briers and thorns.

title: Isaiah 7:25
text: And all the hills that were digged with the mattock, thou shalt not come thither for fear of briers and thorns; but it shall be for the sending forth of oxen, and for the treading of sheep.

title: Isaiah 8:1
text: And Jehovah said unto me, Take thee a great tablet, and write upon it with the pen of a man, For Maher-shalal-hash-baz;

title: Isaiah 8:2
text: and I will take unto me faithful witnesses to record, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.

title: Isaiah 8:3
text: And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said Jehovah unto me, Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

title: Isaiah 8:4
text: For before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and, My mother, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be carried away before the king of Assyria.

title: Isaiah 8:5
text: And Jehovah spake unto me yet again, saying,

title: Isaiah 8:6
text: Forasmuch as this people have refused the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah's son;

title: Isaiah 8:7
text: now therefore, behold, the Lord bringeth up upon them the waters of the River, strong and many, [even] the king of Assyria and all his glory: and it shall come up over all its channels, and go over all its banks;

title: Isaiah 8:8
text: and it shall sweep onward into Judah; it shall overflow and pass through; it shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of its wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel.

title: Isaiah 8:9
text: Make an uproar, O ye peoples, and be broken in pieces; and give ear, all ye of far countries: gird yourselves, and be broken in pieces; gird yourselves, and be broken in pieces.

title: Isaiah 8:10
text: Take counsel together, and it shall be brought to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us.

title: Isaiah 8:11
text: For Jehovah spake thus to me with a strong hand, and instructed me not to walk in the way of this people, saying,

title: Isaiah 8:12
text: Say ye not, A conspiracy, concerning all whereof this people shall say, A conspiracy; neither fear ye their fear, nor be in dread [thereof] .

title: Isaiah 8:13
text: Jehovah of hosts, him shall ye sanctify; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.

title: Isaiah 8:14
text: And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

title: Isaiah 8:15
text: And many shall stumble thereon, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken.

title: Isaiah 8:16
text: Bind thou up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.

title: Isaiah 8:17
text: And I will wait for Jehovah, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him.

title: Isaiah 8:18
text: Behold, I and the children whom Jehovah hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from Jehovah of hosts, who dwelleth in mount Zion.

title: Isaiah 8:19
text: And when they shall say unto you, Seek unto them that have familiar spirits and unto the wizards, that chirp and that mutter: should not a people seek unto their God? on behalf of the living [should they seek] unto the dead?

title: Isaiah 8:20
text: To the law and to the testimony! if they speak not according to this word, surely there is no morning for them.

title: Isaiah 8:21
text: And they shall pass through it, sore distressed and hungry; and it shall come to pass that, when they shall be hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse by their king and by their God, and turn their faces upward:

title: Isaiah 8:22
text: and they shall look unto the earth, and behold, distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish; and into thick darkness [they shall be] driven away.

title: Isaiah 9:1
text: But there shall be no gloom to her that was in anguish. In the former time he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time hath he made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.

title: Isaiah 9:2
text: The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwelt in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.

title: Isaiah 9:3
text: Thou hast multiplied the nation, thou hast increased their joy: they joy before thee according to the joy in harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the spoil.

title: Isaiah 9:4
text: For the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, thou hast broken as in the day of Midian.

title: Isaiah 9:5
text: For all the armor of the armed man in the tumult, and the garments rolled in blood, shall be for burning, for fuel of fire.

title: Isaiah 9:6
text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given; and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

title: Isaiah 9:7
text: Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of Jehovah of hosts will perform this.

title: Isaiah 9:8
text: The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.

title: Isaiah 9:9
text: And all the people shall know, [even] Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria, that say in pride and in stoutness of heart,

title: Isaiah 9:10
text: The bricks are fallen, but we will build with hewn stone; the sycomores are cut down, but we will put cedars in their place.

title: Isaiah 9:11
text: Therefore Jehovah will set up on high against him the adversaries of Rezin, and will stir up his enemies,

title: Isaiah 9:12
text: the Syrians before, and the Philistines behind; and they shall devour Israel with open mouth. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

title: Isaiah 9:13
text: Yet the people have not turned unto him that smote them, neither have they sought Jehovah of hosts.

title: Isaiah 9:14
text: Therefore Jehovah will cut off from Israel head and tail, palm-branch and rush, in one day.

title: Isaiah 9:15
text: The elder and the honorable man, he is the head; and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail.

title: Isaiah 9:16
text: For they that lead this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.

title: Isaiah 9:17
text: Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, neither will he have compassion on their fatherless and widows; for every one is profane and an evil-doer, and every mouth speaketh folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

title: Isaiah 9:18
text: For wickedness burneth as the fire; it devoureth the briers and thorns; yea, it kindleth in the thickets of the forest, and they roll upward in a column of smoke.

title: Isaiah 9:19
text: Through the wrath of Jehovah of hosts is the land burnt up; and the people are as the fuel of fire: no man spareth his brother.

title: Isaiah 9:20
text: And one shall snatch on the right hand, and be hungry; and he shall eat on the left hand, and they shall not be satisfied: they shall eat every man the flesh of his own arm:

title: Isaiah 9:21
text: Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh; and they together shall be against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

title: Isaiah 10:1
text: Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers that write perverseness;

title: Isaiah 10:2
text: to turn aside the needy from justice, and to rob the poor of my people of their right, that widows may be their spoil, and that they may make the fatherless their prey!

title: Isaiah 10:3
text: And what will ye do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which shall come from far? to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glory?

title: Isaiah 10:4
text: They shall only bow down under the prisoners, and shall fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

title: Isaiah 10:5
text: Ho Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, the staff in whose hand is mine indignation!

title: Isaiah 10:6
text: I will send him against a profane nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.

title: Isaiah 10:7
text: Howbeit he meaneth not so, neither doth his heart think so; but it is in his heart to destroy, and to cut off nations not a few.

title: Isaiah 10:8
text: For he saith, Are not my princes all of them kings?

title: Isaiah 10:9
text: Is not Calno as Carchemish? is not Hamath as Arpad? is not Samaria as Damascus?

title: Isaiah 10:10
text: As my hand hath found the kingdoms of the idols, whose graven images did excel them of Jerusalem and of Samaria;

title: Isaiah 10:11
text: shall I not, as I have done unto Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?

title: Isaiah 10:12
text: Wherefore it shall come to pass, that, when the Lord hath performed his whole work upon mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of his high looks.

title: Isaiah 10:13
text: For he hath said, By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I have understanding: and I have removed the bounds of the peoples, and have robbed their treasures, and like a valiant man I have brought down them that sit [on thrones] :

title: Isaiah 10:14
text: and my hand hath found as a nest the riches of the peoples; and as one gathereth eggs that are forsaken, have I gathered all the earth: and there was none that moved the wing, or that opened the mouth, or chirped.

title: Isaiah 10:15
text: Shall the axe boast itself against him that heweth therewith? shall the saw magnify itself against him that wieldeth it? as if a rod should wield them that lift it up, [or] as if a staff should lift up [him that is] not wood.

title: Isaiah 10:16
text: Therefore will the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory there shall be kindled a burning like the burning of fire.

title: Isaiah 10:17
text: And the light of Israel will be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame; and it will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day.

title: Isaiah 10:18
text: And he will consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field, both soul and body: and it shall be as when a standard-bearer fainteth.

title: Isaiah 10:19
text: And the remnant of the trees of his forest shall be few, so that a child may write them.

title: Isaiah 10:20
text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the remnant of Israel, and they that are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more again lean upon him that smote them, but shall lean upon Jehovah, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.

title: Isaiah 10:21
text: A remnant shall return, [even] the remnant of Jacob, unto the mighty God.

title: Isaiah 10:22
text: For though thy people, Israel, be as the sand of the sea, [only] a remnant of them shall return: a destruction [is] determined, overflowing with righteousness.

title: Isaiah 10:23
text: For a full end, and that determined, will the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, make in the midst of all the earth.

title: Isaiah 10:24
text: Therefore thus saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, O my people that dwellest in Zion, be not afraid of the Assyrian, though he smite thee with the rod, and lift up his staff against thee, after the manner of Egypt.

title: Isaiah 10:25
text: For yet a very little while, and the indignation [against thee] shall be accomplished, and mine anger [shall be directed] to his destruction.

title: Isaiah 10:26
text: And Jehovah of hosts will stir up against him a scourge, as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb: and his rod will be over the sea, and he will lift it up after the manner of Egypt. [

title: Isaiah 10:27
text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that his burden shall depart from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed by reason of fatness.

title: Isaiah 10:28
text: He is come to Aiath, he is passed through Migron; at Michmash he layeth up his baggage;

title: Isaiah 10:29
text: they are gone over the pass; they have taken up their lodging at Geba; Ramah trembleth; Gibeah of Saul is fled.

title: Isaiah 10:30
text: Cry aloud with thy voice, O daughter of Gallim! hearken, O Laishah! O thou poor Anathoth!

title: Isaiah 10:31
text: Madmenah is a fugitive; the inhabitants of Gebim flee for safety.

title: Isaiah 10:32
text: This very day shall he halt at Nob: he shaketh his hand at the mount of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.

title: Isaiah 10:33
text: Behold, the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, will lop the boughs with terror: and the high of stature shall be hewn down, and the lofty shall be brought low.

title: Isaiah 10:34
text: And he will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one.

title: Isaiah 11:1
text: And there shall come forth a shoot out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots shall bear fruit.

title: Isaiah 11:2
text: And the Spirit of Jehovah shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Jehovah.

title: Isaiah 11:3
text: And his delight shall be in the fear of Jehovah; and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither decide after the hearing of his ears;

title: Isaiah 11:4
text: but with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and decide with equity for the meek of the earth; and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.

title: Isaiah 11:5
text: And righteousness shall be the girdle of his waist, and faithfulness the girdle of his loins.

title: Isaiah 11:6
text: And the wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.

title: Isaiah 11:7
text: And the cow and the bear shall feed; their young ones shall lie down together; and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.

title: Isaiah 11:8
text: And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the adder's den.

title: Isaiah 11:9
text: They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain; for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Jehovah, as the waters cover the sea.

title: Isaiah 11:10
text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the root of Jesse, that standeth for an ensign of the peoples, unto him shall the nations seek; and his resting-place shall be glorious.

title: Isaiah 11:11
text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, that shall remain, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.

title: Isaiah 11:12
text: And he will set up an ensign for the nations, and will assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

title: Isaiah 11:13
text: The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and they that vex Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.

title: Isaiah 11:14
text: And they shall fly down upon the shoulder of the Philistines on the west; together shall they despoil the children of the east: they shall put forth their hand upon Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon shall obey them.

title: Isaiah 11:15
text: And Jehovah will utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his scorching wind will he wave his hand over the River, and will smite it into seven streams, and cause men to march over dryshod.

title: Isaiah 11:16
text: And there shall be a highway for the remnant of his people, that shall remain, from Assyria; like as there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.

title: Isaiah 12:1
text: And in that day thou shalt say, I will give thanks unto thee, O Jehovah; for though thou wast angry with me, thine anger is turned away and thou comfortest me.

title: Isaiah 12:2
text: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and will not be afraid; for Jehovah, [even] Jehovah, is my strength and song; and he is become my salvation.

title: Isaiah 12:3
text: Therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation.

title: Isaiah 12:4
text: And in that day shall ye say, Give thanks unto Jehovah, call upon his name, declare his doings among the peoples, make mention that his name is exalted.

title: Isaiah 12:5
text: Sing unto Jehovah; for he hath done excellent things: let this be known in all the earth.

title: Isaiah 12:6
text: Cry aloud and shout, thou inhabitant of Zion; for great in the midst of thee is the Holy One of Israel.

title: Isaiah 13:1
text: The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see.

title: Isaiah 13:2
text: Set ye up an ensign upon the bare mountain, lift up the voice unto them, wave the hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles.

title: Isaiah 13:3
text: I have commanded my consecrated ones, yea, I have called my mighty men for mine anger, even my proudly exulting ones.

title: Isaiah 13:4
text: The noise of a multitude in the mountains, as of a great people! the noise of a tumult of the kingdoms of the nations gathered together! Jehovah of hosts is mustering the host for the battle.

title: Isaiah 13:5
text: They come from a far country, from the uttermost part of heaven, even Jehovah, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.

title: Isaiah 13:6
text: Wail ye; for the day of Jehovah is at hand; as destruction from the Almighty shall it come.

title: Isaiah 13:7
text: Therefore shall all hands be feeble, and every heart of man shall melt:

title: Isaiah 13:8
text: and they shall be dismayed; pangs and sorrows shall take hold [of them] ; they shall be in pain as a woman in travail: they shall look in amazement one at another; their faces [shall be] faces of flame.

title: Isaiah 13:9
text: Behold, the day of Jehovah cometh, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy the sinners thereof out of it.

title: Isaiah 13:10
text: For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light; the sun shall be darkened in its going forth, and the moon shall not cause its light to shine.

title: Isaiah 13:11
text: And I will punish the world for [their] evil, and the wicked for their iniquity: and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease, and will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible.

title: Isaiah 13:12
text: I will make a man more rare than fine gold, even a man than the pure gold of Ophir.

title: Isaiah 13:13
text: Therefore I will make the heavens to tremble, and the earth shall be shaken out of its place, in the wrath of Jehovah of hosts, and in the day of his fierce anger.

title: Isaiah 13:14
text: And it shall come to pass, that as the chased roe, and as sheep that no man gathereth, they shall turn every man to his own people, and shall flee every man to his own land.

title: Isaiah 13:15
text: Every one that is found shall be thrust through; and every one that is taken shall fall by the sword.

title: Isaiah 13:16
text: Their infants also shall be dashed in pieces before their eyes; their houses shall be rifled, and their wives ravished.

title: Isaiah 13:17
text: Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, who shall not regard silver, and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.

title: Isaiah 13:18
text: And [their] bows shall dash the young men in pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.

title: Isaiah 13:19
text: And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldeans' pride, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

title: Isaiah 13:20
text: It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation: neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there; neither shall shepherds make their flocks to lie down there.

title: Isaiah 13:21
text: But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there; and their houses shall be full of doleful creatures; and ostriches shall dwell there, and wild goats shall dance there.

title: Isaiah 13:22
text: And wolves shall cry in their castles, and jackals in the pleasant palaces: and her time is near to come, and her days shall not be prolonged.

title: Isaiah 14:1
text: For Jehovah will have compassion on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the sojourner shall join himself with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.

title: Isaiah 14:2
text: And the peoples shall take them, and bring them to their place; and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of Jehovah for servants and for handmaids: and they shall take them captive whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.

title: Isaiah 14:3
text: And it shall come to pass in the day that Jehovah shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy trouble, and from the hard service wherein thou wast made to serve,

title: Isaiah 14:4
text: that thou shalt take up this parable against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!

title: Isaiah 14:5
text: Jehovah hath broken the staff of the wicked, the sceptre of the rulers;

title: Isaiah 14:6
text: that smote the peoples in wrath with a continual stroke, that ruled the nations in anger, with a persecution that none restrained.

title: Isaiah 14:7
text: The whole earth is at rest, [and] is quiet: they break forth into singing.

title: Isaiah 14:8
text: Yea, the fir-trees rejoice at thee, [and] the cedars of Lebanon, [saying], Since thou art laid low, no hewer is come up against us.

title: Isaiah 14:9
text: Sheol from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming; it stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth; it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.

title: Isaiah 14:10
text: All they shall answer and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?

title: Isaiah 14:11
text: Thy pomp is brought down to Sheol, [and] the noise of thy viols: the worm is spread under thee, and worms cover thee.

title: Isaiah 14:12
text: How art thou fallen from heaven, O day-star, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, that didst lay low the nations!

title: Isaiah 14:13
text: And thou saidst in thy heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God; and I will sit upon the mount of congregation, in the uttermost parts of the north;
